# Parallel Review Plan

Receive plan artifacts as read-only input and produce structured findings conforming to `review-findings.schema.json`. Designed for vendor-diverse dispatch — any LLM agent can execute this skill.

## Arguments

`$ARGUMENTS` - OpenSpec change-id to review (e.g., "add-user-authentication")

Optional flags:
- `--adversarial` — Use adversarial review mode: challenges design decisions instead of standard review

## Prerequisites

- OpenSpec proposal exists at `openspec/changes/<change-id>/`
- Proposal has been generated by `/parallel-plan-feature` or `/linear-plan-feature`

## Provider-Neutral Dispatch

Plan review uses the provider-neutral dispatch adapter/configuration path as
the canonical cross-provider mechanism. Claude Code, Codex, Antigravity, Grok,
and Pi are first-class reviewers when configured; provider-specific CLI or
harness details stay inside their adapters.

## Input (Read-Only)

The reviewer receives these artifacts as context but MUST NOT modify them:

- `openspec/changes/<change-id>/proposal.md`
- `openspec/changes/<change-id>/design.md`
- `openspec/changes/<change-id>/tasks.md`
- `openspec/changes/<change-id>/specs/**/spec.md`
- `openspec/changes/<change-id>/contracts/` (if present)
- `openspec/changes/<change-id>/work-packages.yaml` (if present)

## Eight-Axis Finding Schema

Every finding produced by this skill MUST be classified into BOTH dimensions below. The JSON Schema at `openspec/schemas/review-findings.schema.json` enforces both fields as `required` — output that omits either is rejected by the validator in Step 4.

### Eight Axes (the `axis` field)

Five axes adopted from the `code-review-and-quality` reference skill, plus three fitness-function axes. Pick exactly one:

| Axis | What it covers |
|---|---|
| `correctness` | Does the plan, when implemented, produce the right answer? Bugs, off-by-one, missing requirements, ambiguous SHALL clauses. |
| `readability` | Will a future reader understand intent? Naming, structure, spec clarity, ambiguous prose. |
| `architecture` | Does the design fit the system? Module boundaries, layering, coupling, dependency direction, contract shape. |
| `security` | Does the plan introduce or fail to prevent security risk? Auth gaps, input-validation holes, secret handling, OWASP categories. |
| `performance` | Will the implementation be fast and scalable enough? N+1, unbounded queries, missing pagination, hot-path allocations. |
| `observability` | Can the running system be understood from the outside? Missing logs/metrics/traces, unactionable errors, no way to detect the failure mode the plan introduces. |
| `resilience` | Does it degrade safely? Missing retries/timeouts/backoff, unbounded blast radius, no fallback, undefined partial-failure behavior. |
| `compatibility` | Does it stay compatible with what already exists? Breaking API/schema/CLI changes, missing migration path, version or platform assumptions. |

The legacy `type` enum (`spec_gap`, `contract_mismatch`, etc. — see Step 3) is preserved for backward compatibility; `axis` is the new mandatory categorization that all reviewers — human or vendor — must agree on.

### Five Severity Prefixes (the `severity` field)

Every finding's `description` MUST begin with one of these markers. The `severity` enum value MUST match the prefix.

| Prefix | Severity value | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `Critical` | `critical` | Blocks merge. Must be fixed before implementation begins (or before the PR merges). |
| `Nit` | `nit` | Should fix but does not block. Quality, naming, minor structure. |
| `Optional` | `optional` | Consider it. Author may accept or reject without further discussion. |
| `FYI` | `fyi` | Informational. Surfaces context the author may not have known; no action required. |
| `none` | `none` | Positive observation. Names what the plan got right so good patterns survive review. |

Example finding (note prefix and matching `severity`):

```json
{
  "id": 1,
  "axis": "security",
  "severity": "critical",
  "type": "security",
  "criticality": "high",
  "description": "Critical: Requirement R3 admits unauthenticated DELETE on /v1/users/{id} — missing auth precondition.",
  "resolution": "Add a SHALL clause requiring an authenticated session with role=admin before the DELETE handler executes.",
  "disposition": "fix"
}
```

Reviewers MUST NOT collapse multiple severities onto one finding (split them). Reviewers MUST NOT use a severity that contradicts the `disposition` (e.g., `severity: critical` with `disposition: accept` is incoherent — escalate instead).

## Steps

### 1. Load Review Context

Read all plan artifacts listed above. Build a mental model of:
- What the feature does (proposal.md)
- How it will be built (design.md)
- What requirements it satisfies (specs/)
- How work is decomposed (tasks.md, work-packages.yaml)

### 2. Review Checklist

Evaluate the plan against these dimensions:

#### Specification Completeness
- [ ] All requirements use SHALL/MUST language
- [ ] Requirements are testable and verifiable
- [ ] No ambiguous or vague terms

#### Contract Consistency
- [ ] OpenAPI schemas match spec requirements
- [ ] Database schemas support all declared operations
- [ ] Event schemas cover all async flows
- [ ] Generated types match OpenAPI definitions

#### Architecture Alignment
- [ ] Design follows existing codebase patterns
- [ ] No unnecessary dependencies introduced
- [ ] Error handling strategy is complete
- [ ] Migration path is reversible

#### Security Review
- [ ] Input validation at system boundaries
- [ ] Authentication/authorization for new endpoints
- [ ] No secrets in configuration or code
- [ ] OWASP top-10 considerations addressed

#### Performance Review
- [ ] No unbounded queries or loops in design
- [ ] List operations have pagination or size limits
- [ ] Synchronous operations that should be async are identified
- [ ] Caching strategy defined for hot paths (if applicable)
- [ ] Rate limiting considered for public endpoints

#### Observability Review
- [ ] Monitoring requirements defined for new services/endpoints
- [ ] Structured logging requirements for key operations
- [ ] Alerting criteria specified for failure conditions
- [ ] Health/readiness endpoint requirements for new services

#### Compatibility Review
- [ ] Breaking changes to existing APIs are identified and justified
- [ ] Data migration plan is reversible (rollback path exists)
- [ ] Consumer impact analysis for changed interfaces
- [ ] Deprecation notices for removed or changed APIs

#### Resilience Review
- [ ] Retry/timeout/fallback requirements for external dependencies
- [ ] Failure mode analysis for critical paths
- [ ] Idempotency requirements for operations that may be retried
- [ ] Graceful degradation strategy when dependencies are unavailable

#### Work Package Validity (if work-packages.yaml exists)
- [ ] DAG has no cycles
- [ ] Parallel packages have non-overlapping write scopes
- [ ] Lock keys follow canonicalization rules
- [ ] Verification steps are appropriate for each package tier
- [ ] Integration package depends on all implementation packages

### 3. Produce Findings

Generate findings as a JSON array conforming to `review-findings.schema.json`:

```json
{
  "review_type": "plan",
  "target": "<change-id>",
  "reviewer_vendor": "<model-name>",
  "findings": [
    {
      "id": 1,
      "type": "spec_gap",
      "criticality": "high",
      "description": "Requirement R3 lacks error handling specification for 429 rate limit responses",
      "resolution": "Add a requirement specifying retry-after header handling",
      "disposition": "fix"
    }
  ]
}
```

#### Finding Types
- `spec_gap` — Missing or incomplete requirements
- `contract_mismatch` — Inconsistency between contracts and specs
- `architecture` — Design pattern or structural concern
- `security` — Security vulnerability or missing protection
- `performance` — Potential performance issue
- `style` — Code style or convention violation
- `correctness` — Logical error in the plan
- `observability` — Missing monitoring, logging, or alerting requirements
- `compatibility` — Breaking change to existing API or missing migration plan
- `resilience` — Missing retry, timeout, or fallback requirements

#### Dispositions
- `fix` — Author should fix before implementation
- `regenerate` — Artifact needs regeneration (e.g., contract schema mismatch)
- `accept` — Minor issue, acceptable as-is
- `escalate` — Requires human decision or cross-team coordination

### 4. Validate Output

Validate the findings JSON against `openspec/schemas/review-findings.schema.json`:

```bash
# Quick validation
python3 -c "
import json, jsonschema
schema = json.load(open('openspec/schemas/review-findings.schema.json'))
findings = json.load(open('<findings-output-path>'))
jsonschema.validate(findings, schema)
print('Valid')
"
```

### 5. Submit Findings

Write findings to `openspec/changes/<change-id>/review-findings-plan.json`.

If `CAN_HANDOFF=true`, write a review handoff with:
- Summary of critical/high findings
- Overall disposition recommendation (proceed/revise/block)

### 6. Dispatch Multi-Vendor Reviews

After writing your own findings, dispatch reviews to other vendor CLIs and synthesize consensus.

**Write the review prompt** to `openspec/changes/<change-id>/reviews/review-prompt.md` — include instructions to read the plan artifacts and output only valid JSON conforming to `review-findings.schema.json`. The required-field list and enums MUST come from `review_findings_schema.prompt_contract()` / `prompt_contract_block()` — do not hand-copy the field list.

**Adversarial mode**: If `--adversarial` flag was passed, wrap the review prompt with adversarial framing before dispatch:

```python
from adversarial_prompt import wrap_adversarial
prompt = wrap_adversarial(prompt)  # Prepends contrarian persona instructions
```

The dispatch still uses `--mode review` (unchanged) — only the prompt content differs. Adversarial findings flow through the same consensus pipeline with equal weight (Design Decision D1).

**Dispatch to other vendors** (excluding the current agent's vendor):

```bash
python3 "<skill-base-dir>/../parallel-infrastructure/scripts/review_dispatcher.py" \
  --review-type plan \
  --mode review \
  --prompt-file "openspec/changes/<change-id>/reviews/review-prompt.md" \
  --cwd "$(pwd)" \
  --output-dir "openspec/changes/<change-id>/reviews" \
  --exclude-vendor claude_code \
  --timeout 600
```

This dispatches to all available vendors configured in `agents.yaml` with `cli` sections. Each vendor runs independently and writes findings to `reviews/findings-<vendor>-plan.json`.

**Agent discovery resolution chain**: An explicit `--agents-yaml` wins. Otherwise the dispatcher searches from the reviewed `--cwd` for checkout-local `agent-coordinator/agents.yaml`, then tries the configured coordination MCP/HTTP roster, and finally the process/global disk fallback. SDK-only coordinator rosters count as configured and are not discarded. Dispatch, `--check-vendors`, and `--list-agents` use this same resolver. Use `--list-agents --cwd <reviewed-checkout>` to verify the exact roster.

**Troubleshooting dispatch failures**: Run `python3 <script> --list-agents` to verify agent discovery. Common issues: (1) `~/.claude.json` has no `mcpServers.coordination` entry — run `/setup-coordinator`, (2) async/remote agents may time out — local agents are more reliable, (3) some vendors may return non-JSON output — check `review-manifest.json` for error details.

**Synthesize consensus** from all findings (yours + vendor results):

```bash
python3 "<skill-base-dir>/../parallel-infrastructure/scripts/consensus_synthesizer.py" \
  --review-type plan \
  --target "<change-id>" \
  --findings "openspec/changes/<change-id>/review-findings-plan.json" \
             "openspec/changes/<change-id>/reviews/findings-"*"-plan.json" \
  --output "openspec/changes/<change-id>/reviews/consensus-plan.json"
```

**Present consensus summary** to the user:
- Confirmed findings (2+ vendors agree) — high confidence, may block
- Unconfirmed findings (single vendor) — lower confidence, warnings
- Disagreements (vendors disagree on disposition) — escalate to human

If no other vendors are available (CLIs not installed), skip this step and proceed with single-vendor findings only.

## Output

- `openspec/changes/<change-id>/review-findings-plan.json` — your findings
- `openspec/changes/<change-id>/reviews/findings-<vendor>-plan.json` — per-vendor findings
- `openspec/changes/<change-id>/reviews/consensus-plan.json` — synthesized consensus
- `openspec/changes/<change-id>/reviews/review-manifest.json` — dispatch metadata

## Design for Vendor Diversity

This skill is intentionally simple and self-contained so it can be dispatched to any LLM agent:
- No coordinator dependencies required
- All input is file-based (read-only)
- Output is a single JSON file with a well-defined schema
- No side effects (no git commits, no lock acquisition)

When this skill is dispatched *to* another vendor by the orchestrator, only Steps 1-5 run (the vendor produces findings). Step 6 (multi-vendor dispatch) only runs when this skill is the *primary* reviewer — i.e., when invoked directly by the user or the orchestrating agent.

## Common Rationalizations

| Rationalization | Why it's wrong |
|---|---|
| "I only found one issue, so I'll skip the axis/severity classification — the description is enough" | The schema rejects findings without `axis` and `severity`; cross-vendor consensus relies on these fields to match equivalent findings. Skipping = the dispatcher discards your review. |
| "This finding spans two axes — I'll just pick one" | Pick the dominant axis and split the rest into separate findings. Mashing two axes into one description means consensus matching cannot deduplicate against another vendor who split them. |
| "The plan looks fine — I'll just emit zero findings" | A review with zero findings is suspicious. At minimum, emit `severity: none` positive observations naming what the plan got right; this signals the review actually happened rather than timed out. |
| "The orchestrator will catch contradictions between `severity` and `disposition`" | It won't — the orchestrator routes by `disposition`. Inconsistent severity/disposition pairs survive into the consensus and confuse downstream automation. Make them coherent at write time. |

## Red Flags

- A `review-findings-plan.json` file with findings that lack the `axis` field — the schema validation step (Step 4) was skipped or its output ignored.
- Every finding has the same severity (e.g., everything is `Critical`). A real review covers a spectrum; uniform severity means the reviewer wasn't actually grading.
- Description prose does NOT start with the matching severity prefix (`Critical:` / `Nit:` / `Optional:` / `FYI:` / nothing-for-`none`). The prefix is the human-readable signal; if it disagrees with the enum value, the reviewer wrote the JSON without re-reading the prose.
- A `security`-axis finding with `disposition: accept`. Security findings are never silently accepted; if the risk is real, the disposition must be `fix` or `escalate`.
- Findings reference file paths or line ranges that don't exist in the plan artifacts (proposal/design/specs). The reviewer hallucinated context.

## Verification

1. Run the JSON Schema validator from Step 4 and confirm `Valid` — this proves `axis` and `severity` are present on every finding.
2. Spot-check 3 findings: confirm the `description` text begins with the prefix matching the `severity` enum value (e.g., `severity: critical` ↔ description starts with `Critical:`).
3. Confirm at least two different `axis` values appear across the findings array (a single-axis review missed the other seven dimensions of the schema).
4. Confirm `disposition` is coherent with `severity`: `critical`/`nit` → `fix`; `optional`/`fyi` → `accept`; `none` → `accept`; mismatches must be `escalate` with a justification in `resolution`.
5. Confirm `reviewer_vendor` is populated — anonymous findings cannot participate in consensus.

A new\noptional `routing_profile` is strict (`extra=forbid`) and types:\n\n- expected duration seconds;\n- scope category (`read-only|bounded-write|broad-write`);\n- interactivity (`interactive|headless`);\n- secret need category (`none|brokered|direct`), never a secret value;\n- positive parallelism;\n- repository shape (`single-package|monorepo|unknown`);\n- roadmap-policy constraints (allowed/excluded lane/vendor sets and an allowed-location set);\n- optional required location, isolation, and dispatch mode.\n\nPydantic validates the external boundary and FastAPI/MCP share the same request model.\nNew response objects are optional-with-default for legacy validation but are always\npopulated by a successful DG-04 service decision.\n\n## D3 — Rules are ordered, typed, and versioned\n\n`agent-coordinator/routing.yaml` carries `schema_version`, `policy_version`,\ndispatch-mode defaults, ordered first-match constraint rules, and a local-fallback\ndimension table. A dedicated loader validates unknown fields, duplicate IDs, enum values,\nranges, and phase dispatch defaults, then records a SHA-256 checksum of canonical file\nbytes.\n\nEach rule has a typed `when` predicate over the profile and a typed `constrain` block for\nlocation, isolation, and dispatch mode. Explicit request constraints take precedence;\notherwise the first matching rule that mentions a dimension constrains that dimension.\nThe phase-specific or global dispatch default is used only when no explicit or rule-based\ndispatch mode exists; unmatched location/isolation remain unconstrained. Rules narrow\nfeasibility and never add a second utility score. Changing a rule therefore changes the\nfeasible assignment set without code edits.\n\nThe Docker image copies the file beside `agents.yaml` and the loader resolves it from\n`ROUTING_CONFIG` or the package root, never the process working directory.\n\n## D4 — DG-01 is the only lane source and joins are exact\n\n`RoutingService` injects/loads `VendorRegistryService` in process and requests all\nlanes without `available_only` prefiltering so exclusion provenance is retained. For\neach lane it consumes dg-01's projected catalog models. Agent-name suffixes, provider/publisher guesses, substring matches,\nand fuzzy model names are forbidden. Missing or ambiguous projections remain explicit\nregistry misses and never become routable candidates.\n\nA watchdog `ConfiguredCatalogSync` job materializes configured non-OpenRouter lane\nmodels in `model_catalog`. `agents.yaml` explicitly sets `catalog_vendor` and\n`endpoint_kind` for those lanes: local subscription CLIs use their exact vendor type plus\n`vendor-cli`; remote SDK lanes use their exact vendor type plus `vendor-sdk`. CLI model\nIDs come from the canonical provider model map; SDK model IDs come only from the lane's\nSDK model/fallback list. The job inserts only missing identity rows, with enabled catalog\navailability and unknown price/posterior, and never overwrites existing pricing,\nposterior, availability, or refresh data. Registry probe/rate-limit state remains the live\nlane-availability source.\n\nOpenRouter/local catalog rows remain owned by their existing refresh/probe jobs; for a\nmulti-publisher OpenRouter lane, exact model/endpoint/base-URL matching must yield one row\nbefore the row's catalog vendor becomes part of the four-field key. Missing or ambiguous\nidentity metadata is an explicit configuration miss, never filled from an agent-name\nsuffix or publisher guess. The registry and catalog snapshots are\neach loaded once per request. A registry read or shape failure fails closed as\n`routing-registry-unavailable`; it never falls back to catalog-only scoring. Catalog rows\nwith no exact configured lane projection are retained in `excluded` as\n`catalog:no-configured-lane`, rather than disappearing silently.\n\n## D5 — Feasibility precedes DG-00 utility\n\nFor each exact lane/model pair, pure feasibility checks apply in deterministic order:\n\n1. live lane availability and lane/model rate limits;\n2. dispatchability, archetype, and requested/default dispatch mode;\n3. explicit/configured location and isolation constraints;\n4. roadmap-policy allow/exclude sets;\n5. catalog availability and dg-00 modality/quota constraints.\n\nReasons are machine-readable and sanitized. DG-00's existing `unavailable` and\n`quota:exhausted` values remain accepted alongside DG-04's namespaced reasons. Only feasible lane/model candidates enter\nthe existing `score_and_rank`; DG-04 does not duplicate quality, posterior, cost,\nlatency, headroom, or exploration math. Multiple lanes may project the same catalog\nmodel, so the final stable order is `(-score, agent_id, catalog identity)`.\nLocation and isolation constraints use exact equality and dispatch mode uses exact\nmembership in the lane's configured modes; DG-04 does not infer an isolation-strength\nordering.\n\n## D6 — Assignment and provenance are additive\n\nA successful response adds top-level:\n\n- `assignment`: exact `agent_id`, `vendor_type`, `policy_vendor`,\n  `catalog_vendor`, location, isolation, dispatch mode, model, endpoint kind, and base\n  URL;\n- `provenance`: source (`coordinator` or `local-static`), policy version/checksum,\n  matched rule IDs, rationale, persistence flag, durable-audit flag, and exact\n  lane/catalog key.\n\nThe selected candidate and every alternative carry their own additive `assignment`, while\nthe response retains the selected candidate's assignment/provenance at top level for\nconvenience. Existing selected-candidate fields remain intact for older consumers.\nExcluded assignments use a typed shape containing lane/catalog identity and a bounded\nmachine-readable reason.\n\n## D7 — Durable routing record is authoritative; audit event is linked\n\nThe existing `routing_decisions` row is the authoritative durable routing audit. Its\nsanitized `request` stores only declared task signals and the strict routing profile;\npermissive legacy extras such as `write_allow` are never persisted. Its `selected` object\nstores selected assignment plus provenance, and every item in `alternatives` stores its\nown assignment. `excluded` stores typed exclusion records. These are additive JSONB\nshapes and require no new table columns.\n\nMigration `042_atomic_routing_audit.sql` adds one transaction-scoped RPC that inserts the\n`routing_decisions` row and a sanitized link-only `routing_decision` audit-log event\natomically. The event contains only decision ID, selected agent/model, routing-policy\nversion/checksum, source, and success. The service awaits the RPC result and returns only\nafter both rows commit. Its catalog key is null because no live catalog join occurred. A local\nUUID is explicitly not retrievable from coordinator decision storage. Missing or invalid\nconfiguration fails loud; the helper does not invent permissive defaults.\n\nThe fallback table's order is only a deterministic choice among the lane's exact\nconfigured values while the coordinator is unreachable. It is not an isolation-strength\nprecedence or enforcement policy. The reusable helper lives in\n`skills/coordination-bridge/scripts/routing_fallback.py`, resolves repository config from\nan explicit root or discovered checkout root, and is used by bridge and HTTP-proxy\ndegradation paths.\n\nThe existing `resolve_archetype_for_phase` fallback is not rewritten: disabled,\nfailure, malformed-response, and timeout paths still return the exact dg-00 static\n`ResolvedArchetype` object with no added reasons or fields.\n\n## D9 — DG-05/DG-06 boundaries remain closed\n\nDG-04 carries the lane's current configured isolation as data and may filter an explicit\nrequest. openspec/changes/implement-the-task-router-vendor-x-location-x-model/reviews/round-3/raw-pi-plan.txt:175:{"type":"message_start","message":{"role":"toolResult","toolCallId":"chatcmpl-tool-e0689e421fe34f0d9d63ab45a11571a8","toolName":"read","content":[{"type":"text","text":"# Design: extend routing to vendor × location × isolation × dispatch mode\n\n## D1 — Extend one resolver and one public operation\n\nDG-04 extends the dg-00 `RoutingService.select_model()` pipeline, HTTP\n`POST /routing/select_model`, and MCP `select_model_for_task`. It does not add\n`POST /route/task`, a second score function, or a second routing decision store.\nThe existing `selected.vendor/model/endpoint_kind` meaning remains observable and\nunchanged; assignment and provenance are additive fields.\n\n## D2 — Preserve compatibility with an optional strict profile\n\nLegacy `task_signals` remains accepted with its current permissive extra-field\nbehavior because existing phase callers send fields such as `write_allow`. A new\noptional `routing_profile` is strict (`extra=forbid`) and types:\n\n- expected duration seconds;\n- scope category (`read-only|bounded-write|broad-write`);\n- interactivity (`interactive|headless`);\n- secret need category (`none|brokered|direct`), never a secret value;\n- positive parallelism;\n- repository shape (`single-package|monorepo|unknown`);\n- roadmap-policy constraints (allowed/excluded lane/vendor sets and an allowed-location set);\n- optional required location, isolation, and dispatch mode.\n\nPydantic validates the external boundary and FastAPI/MCP share the same request model.\nNew response objects are optional-with-default for legacy validation but are always\npopulated by a successful DG-04 service decision.\n\n## D3 — Rules are ordered, typed, and versioned\n\n`agent-coordinator/routing.yaml` carries `schema_version`, `policy_version`,\ndispatch-mode defaults, ordered first-match constraint rules, and a local-fallback\ndimension table. A dedicated loader validates unknown fields, duplicate IDs, enum values,\nranges, and phase dispatch defaults, then records a SHA-256 checksum of canonical file\nbytes.\n\nEach rule has a typed `when` predicate over the profile and a typed `constrain` block for\nlocation, isolation, and dispatch mode. Explicit request constraints take precedence;\notherwise the first matching rule that mentions a dimension constrains that dimension.\nThe phase-specific or global dispatch default is used only when no explicit or rule-based\ndispatch mode exists; unmatched location/isolation remain unconstrained. Rules narrow\nfeasibility and never add a second utility score. Changing a rule therefore changes the\nfeasible assignment set without code edits.\n\nThe Docker image copies the file beside `agents.yaml` and the loader resolves it from\n`ROUTING_CONFIG` or the package root, never the process working directory.\n\n## D4 — DG-01 is the only lane source and joins are exact\n\n`RoutingService` injects/loads `VendorRegistryService` in process and requests all\nlanes without `available_only` prefiltering so exclusion provenance is retained. For\neach lane it consumes dg-01's projected catalog models. It forms an assignment only when\nthe catalog candidate identity exactly equals the projection key:\n\n`(catalog_vendor, model, endpoint_kind, base_url)`.\n\n`base_url` and additive lane identity travel through `CandidateInput` and\n`ScoredCandidate`. Agent-name suffixes, provider/publisher guesses, substring matches,\nand fuzzy model names are forbidden. Missing or ambiguous projections remain explicit\nregistry misses and never become routable candidates.\n\nA watchdog `ConfiguredCatalogSync` job materializes configured non-OpenRouter lane\nmodels in `model_catalog`. `agents.yaml` explicitly sets `catalog_vendor` and\n`endpoint_kind` for those lanes: local subscription CLIs use their exact vendor type plus\n`vendor-cli`; remote SDK lanes use their exact vendor type plus `vendor-sdk`. CLI model\nIDs come from the canonical provider model map; SDK model IDs come only from the lane's\nSDK model/fallback list. The job inserts only missing identity rows, with enabled catalog\navailability and unknown price/posterior, and never overwrites existing pricing,\nposterior, availability, or refresh data. Registry probe/rate-limit state remains the live\nlane-availability source.\n\nOpenRouter/local catalog rows remain owned by their existing refresh/probe jobs; for a\nmulti-publisher OpenRouter lane, exact model/endpoint/base-URL matching must yield one row\nbefore the row's catalog vendor becomes part of the four-field key. Missing or ambiguous\nidentity metadata is an explicit configuration miss, never filled from an agent-name\nsuffix or publisher guess. A real-agents.yaml test proves at least one configured CLI\nlane projects exactly after this bootstrap.\n\nThe routing path constructs a read-only `VendorRegistryService(audit=None)` because the\nrouter persists its own typed exclusions and atomic audit link; this avoids emitting one\ngeneric projection-miss audit row per request. The registry and catalog snapshots are\neach loaded once per request. A registry read or shape failure fails closed as\n`routing-registry-unavailable`; it never falls back to catalog-only scoring. Catalog rows\nwith no exact configured lane projection are retained in `excluded` as\n`catalog:no-configured-lane`, rather than disappearing silently.\n\n## D5 — Feasibility precedes DG-00 utility\n\nFor each exact lane/model pair, pure feasibility checks apply in deterministic order:\n\n1. live lane availability and lane/model rate limits;\n2. dispatchability, archetype, and requested/default dispatch mode;\n3. explicit/configured location and isolation constraints;\n4. roadmap-policy allow/exclude sets;\n5. catalog availability and dg-00 modality/quota constraints.\n\nReasons are machine-readable and sanitized. DG-00's existing `unavailable` and\n`quota:exhausted` values remain accepted alongside DG-04's namespaced reasons. Only feasible lane/model candidates enter\nthe existing `score_and_rank`; DG-04 does not duplicate quality, posterior, cost,\nlatency, headroom, or exploration math. Multiple lanes may project the same catalog\nmodel, so the final stable order is `(-score, agent_id, catalog identity)`.\nLocation and isolation constraints use exact equality and dispatch mode uses exact\nmembership in the lane's configured modes; DG-04 does not infer an isolation-strength\nordering.\n\n## D6 — Assignment and provenance are additive\n\nA successful response adds top-level:\n\n- `assignment`: exact `agent_id`, `vendor_type`, `policy_vendor`,\n  `catalog_vendor`, location, isolation, dispatch mode, model, endpoint kind, and base\n  URL;\n- `provenance`: source (`coordinator` or `local-static`), policy version/checksum,\n  matched rule IDs, rationale, persistence flag, durable-audit flag, and exact\n  lane/catalog key.\n\nThe selected candidate and every alternative carry their own additive `assignment`, while\nthe response retains the selected candidate's assignment/provenance at top level for\nconvenience. Existing selected-candidate fields remain intact for older consumers.\nExcluded assignments use a typed shape containing lane/catalog identity and a bounded\nmachine-readable reason.\n\n## D7 — Durable routing record is authoritative; audit event is linked\n\nThe existing `routing_decisions` row is the authoritative durable routing audit. Its\nsanitized `request` stores only declared task signals and the strict routing profile;\npermissive legacy extras such as `write_allow` are never persisted. Its `selected` object\nstores selected assignment plus provenance, and every item in `alternatives` stores its\nown assignment. `excluded` stores typed exclusion records. These are additive JSONB\nshapes and require no new table columns.\n\nMigration `042_atomic_routing_audit.sql` adds one transaction-scoped RPC that inserts the\n`routing_decisions` row and a sanitized link-only `routing_decision` audit-log event\natomically. The event contains only decision ID, selected agent/model, routing-policy\nversion/checksum, source, and success. The service awaits the RPC result and returns only\nafter both rows commit. RPC failure rolls back both writes and produces HTTP 503 detail\n`routing-durability-unavailable`; the MCP mirror returns its existing 503 error envelope.\nFire-and-forget `AuditService.log_operation()` is not used for this invariant, and neither\nan orphan decision nor an orphan audit link is observable. Existing dg-00 callers still\ntake their exact static fallback on any non-200 response.\n\nThe `routing_decisions.policy_version` column keeps dg-00 scorer version\n`linear-utility-v1`; the routing YAML version/checksum live in selected provenance. No raw\nsecret, environment value, prompt, free-form task-signal extra, or unbounded path list\nenters either record; only typed/bounded categories and rationale enter persistence.\n\n## D8 — Local fallback is configuration-derived and honest\n\nA skills-side bridge/helper may fall back only after transport timeout/unreachability. It\nloads the checkout's validated `routing.yaml`, `agents.yaml`, and archetype model map,\nthen combines the caller's already-resolved static provider/model with the fallback\ndimension order. It never embeds a roster, fabricates availability, or performs fuzzy\nassociation.\n\nThe response has the normal assignment shape plus `fallback=true`,\n`source=local-static`, `persisted=false`, `durable_audit=false`, and a bounded\nfailure reason. Its catalog key is null because no live catalog join occurred. A local\nUUID is explicitly not retrievable from coordinator decision storage. Missing or invalid\nconfiguration fails loud; the helper does not invent permissive defaults.\n\nThe fallback table's order is only a deterministic choice among the lane's exact\nconfigured values while the coordinator is unreachable. It is not an isolation-strength\nprecedence or enforcement policy. The reusable helper lives in\n`skills/coordination-bridge/scripts/routing_fallback.py`, resolves repository config from\nan explicit root or discovered checkout root, and is used by bridge and HTTP-proxy\ndegradation paths.\n\nThe existing `resolve_archetype_for_phase` fallback is not rewritten: disabled,\nfailure, malformed-response, and timeout paths still return the exact dg-00 static\n`ResolvedArchetype` object with no added reasons or fields.\n\n## D9 — DG-05/DG-06 boundaries remain closed\n\nDG-04 carries the lane's current configured isolation as data and may filter an explicit\nrequest. It does not define per-mode overrides, the isolation precedence ladder, or\nenforcement; DG-05 owns that contract. It does not call routing before `dispatch_fn`,\nchange `phase_agent.py`, redispatch work, or add loop caps; DG-06 owns obedience.\nNo sandbox is launched; DG-07 owns enforcement.\n\n## D10 — Test-first packages and validation\n\nContract/config tests fail first, followed by pure policy/association tests, then service\nand transport/fallback tests. No dg-05 admission controls or dg-06 approval workflows ✓\n\nLet me check for any gaps or issues.\n\nLooking at the routing.schema.json - the fallback only has location_order and isolation_order, but not dispatch_mode_order. The design says \"The fallback table's order is only a deterministic choice among the lane's exact configured values while the coordinator is unreachable.\" But the schema doesn't include dispatch_mode in fallback. This could be an issue since dispatch_mode is one of the dimensions.\n\nAlso, the routing.yaml schema has phase_dispatch_modes in defaults, but the fallback doesn't include dispatch_mode. The design D3 says \"The phase-specific or global dispatch default is used only when no explicit or rule-based dispatch mode exists; unmatched location/isolation remain unconstrained.\" And D8 says \"The fallback table's order is only a deterministic choice among the lane's exact configured values while the coordinator is unreachable.\" But the schema only has location_order and isolation_order in fallback.\n\nLet me check the design again: \"A dedicated loader validates unknown fields, duplicate IDs, enum values, ranges, and phase dispatch defaults, then records a SHA-256 checksum of canonical file bytes.\" and \"The fallback table's order is only a deterministic choice among the lane's exact configured values while the coordinator is unreachable. It is not an isolation-strength precedence or enforcement policy.\"\n\nThe fallback schema only has location_order and isolation_order. Dispatch mode is handled via phase_dispatch_modes in defaults. So the fallback for dispatch mode would come from the phase defaults. This seems intentional.\n\nAnother thing: The openapi v1.1.yaml has `routing_profile` with `required_location`, `required_isolation`, `required_dispatch_mode` - all optional. But the `TaskRoutingProfile` doesn't have a `required` field - all properties are optional with defaults. This is fine.\n\nLet me check the VendorLane from dg-01: it has `catalog_vendor` as optional (nullable). The design D4 says \"For each lane it consumes dg-01's projected catalog models. It forms an assignment only when the catalog candidate identity exactly equals the projection key: (catalog_vendor, model, endpoint_kind, base_url).\" But if catalog_vendor is nullable in VendorLane, how does this work? The design says \"OpenRouter/local catalog rows remain owned by their existing refresh/probe jobs; for a multi-publisher OpenRouter lane, exact model/endpoint/base-URL matching must yield one row before the row's catalog vendor becomes part of the four-field key.\" So for OpenRouter lanes, the catalog_vendor comes from the catalog row, not from the lane config. For non-OpenRouter lanes, the lane should have catalog_vendor set explicitly in agents.yaml.\n\nThe design also says: \"agents.yaml explicitly sets catalog_vendor and endpoint_kind for those lanes: local subscription CLIs use their exact vendor type plus vendor-cli; remote SDK lanes use their exact vendor type plus vendor-sdk.\" So this is addressed.\n\nNow let me look for potential issues:\n\n1. **routing.yaml fallback missing dispatch_mode** - The schema only has location_order and isolation_order in fallback. The design says fallback uses \"the lane's exact configured values\" but dispatch_mode is not in the fallback ordering. This could be a gap since dispatch_mode is a routing dimension.\n\n2. **The openapi v1.1 Candidate.assignment requires `catalog_vendor` but the dg-01 VendorLane has `catalog_vendor` as nullable** - The assignment schema requires catalog_vendor (it's in required array). But if a lane doesn't have catalog_vendor set (like OpenRouter lanes), how is this handled? The design says for OpenRouter, the catalog_vendor comes from the catalog row match. So it should be populated at routing time. This seems fine.\n\n3. **The routing-decision.schema.json has `source` with const \"coordinator\" and `success` with const true** - This means the audit event only represents successful coordinator decisions. The design says the RPC is atomic and only commits on success. Failed decisions don't create audit events (they return 503). Local fallback doesn't create audit events. This seems correct per design.\n\n4. **Work-packages.yaml wp-policy-service locks `agent-coordinator/src/vendor_registry.py` and `agent-coordinator/src/watchdog.py`** - These are dg-01 files. Since dg-04 depends on dg-01, modifying dg-01 files in dg-04 could be a coupling concern. But the design says the ConfiguredCatalogSync job goes in watchdog.py and the RoutingService uses VendorRegistryService in-process. The watchdog.py changes are for the new job. The vendor_registry.py might need changes to support the in-process usage pattern. This is a cross-cutting concern but may be acceptable.\n\n5. **The design D4 says \"The routing path constructs a read-only VendorRegistryService(audit=None)\"** - This creates a new instance without audit. The VendorRegistryService from dg-01 might not support audit=None parameter. This is an implementation detail but could be a compatibility issue.\n\n6. **The openapi v1.1 SelectModelRequest has `routing_profile` as optional with default null** - But the design says \"A new optional routing_profile is strict (extra=forbid)\". The schema has `additionalProperties: false` on TaskRoutingProfile, which is good. But the routing_profile itself is optional at the request level. This is fine for backward compatibility.\n\n7. **The work-packages.yaml wp-contract-config has `role: contracts-author` but no `archetype`** - Other packages have `archetype: implementer` or `archetype: validator`. This might be intentional since it's a contracts package.\n\n8. **The design D7 says \"The routing_decisions.policy_version column keeps dg-00 scorer version linear-utility-v1; the routing YAML version/checksum live in selected provenance.\"** - This means the database column policy_version is NOT updated to include routing policy version. The routing policy version/checksum is only in the provenance JSONB. This is a design decision that should be explicit. It could be a finding if it's not clearly communicated.\n\n9. **The tasks.md task 1.5 says \"Pin bounded persistence projection, typed exclusions, and exact local-fallback invariants in contracts.\"** - The contracts seem to cover this.\n\n10. **The spec.md says \"A periodic configuration-backed job SHALL materialize missing non-OpenRouter catalog identities from explicit lane metadata and the canonical provider model map without overwriting live catalog observations.\"** - This is the ConfiguredCatalogSync job. The design D4 describes it. The work-packages.yaml includes watchdog.py in wp-policy-service scope. This seems covered.\n\n11. **The openapi v1.1 ExcludedAssignment reason pattern includes `cedar:` prefix** - This is a dg-00 reason. The design says \"DG-00's existing unavailable and quota:exhausted values remain accepted alongside DG-04's namespaced reasons.\" The pattern allows `(lane|policy|catalog|roadmap|registry|cedar):`. This seems correct.\n\n12. **The routing.yaml schema rule.when has minProperties: 1 but no required fields** - This means a rule could have just `phase` or just `scope`, etc. The design says \"Each rule has a typed when predicate over the profile and a typed constrain block\". This seems intentional for flexibility.\n\n13. **The work-packages.yaml wp-integration has `locks: {files: [], keys: [\"feature:task-routing:integration\"]}`** - Empty files lock but a key lock. This is fine for an integration package.\n\n14. **The design D3 says \"The Docker image copies the file beside agents.yaml and the loader resolves it from ROUTING_CONFIG or the package root, never the process working directory.\"** - This is good practice.\n\n15. **The spec.md requirement \"Honest local fallback\" says \"its catalog key SHALL be null because no live catalog join occurred\"** - The openapi RoutingProvenance has catalog_key as nullable array or null. This matches.\n\n16. **The spec.md requirement \"Additive assignment and provenance\" says \"the same decision ID and assignment SHALL be written to routing_decisions\" and \"a link-only coordinator audit event SHALL record decision ID, selected agent/model, routing-policy version/checksum, source, and success\" and \"both records SHALL commit atomically before the response is returned\"** - The design D7 covers this with migration 042 and atomic RPC.\n\n17. **The spec.md requirement \"Registry-backed feasibility precedes utility\" says \"Registry failure fails closed\" and \"Unprojected catalog candidate remains explainable\"** - The design D4 and D5 cover this.\n\nNow, let me identify actual findings that are issues or gaps:\n\n**Finding 1**: The `routing.schema.json` fallback section only defines `location_order` and `isolation_order` but not `dispatch_mode_order`. Since dispatch_mode is a routing dimension (along with location and isolation), the fallback should have a deterministic order for dispatch_mode as well, or explicitly document why it's omitted (e.g., it comes from phase defaults). The design D8 says \"The fallback table's order is only a deterministic choice among the lane's exact configured values\" - this implies all three dimensions. This is a spec_gap.\n\n**Finding 2**: The `routing-decision.schema.json` audit event has `source` with `const: \"coordinator\"` and `success` with `const: true`. This schema cannot represent failed routing decisions or local fallback decisions. While the design says failed decisions return 503 and don't create audit events, and local fallback doesn't create audit events, having a schema that only allows success=true and source=coordinator limits observability. If the requirement is \"honestly linked durable coordinator audit event\", the schema should at least allow success=false for failed atomic commits, or this should be explicitly documented as intentional. This is a potential observability gap.\n\n**Finding 3**: The `wp-policy-service` package locks `agent-coordinator/src/vendor_registry.py` and `agent-coordinator/src/watchdog.py` which are dg-01 files. Since dg-04 is stacked on dg-01, modifying dg-01 files in dg-04 creates a coupling that could complicate merging and testing. The design says \"RoutingService injects/loads VendorRegistryService in process\" - if this requires changes to vendor_registry.py (e.g., adding audit=None constructor parameter), that's a dg-01 interface change. This is an architecture/compatibility concern.\n\n**Finding 4**: The openapi v1.1 `Candidate` schema has `assignment` and `provenance` as optional with default null, but the design says \"New response objects are optional-with-default for legacy validation but are always populated by a successful DG-04 service decision.\" The schema allows null, which is correct for backward compatibility, but there's no way to enforce at the schema level that successful decisions always populate these. This is a runtime guarantee only. This is fine but worth noting as a design choice.\n\n**Finding 5**: The `routing.yaml` schema validation happens in a \"dedicated loader\" (design D3) rather than purely in JSON schema. The JSON schema validates structure but not semantic constraints like \"phase_dispatch_modes references valid phases\" or \"rule IDs are unique\". The design says the loader validates these. This is an implementation concern but the plan should specify that the loader is part of the contract. The tasks.md task 1.3 says \"Define and validate versioned routing.yaml\" - this covers it.\n\n**Finding 6**: The design D4 says \"The routing path constructs a read-only VendorRegistryService(audit=None) because the router persists its own typed exclusions and atomic audit link; this avoids emitting one generic projection-miss audit row per request.\" This implies VendorRegistryService accepts an `audit` parameter. If dg-01's VendorRegistryService doesn't have this parameter, this is a breaking change to dg-01. This needs verification against dg-01's actual interface.\n\n**Finding 7**: The work-packages.yaml has `wp-contract-config` with `role: contracts-author` but no `archetype` field, while other packages have `archetype: implementer` or `archetype: validator`. This might be intentional but could be an inconsistency in the package definition schema.\n\n**Finding 8**: The design D7 says \"The routing_decisions.policy_version column keeps dg-00 scorer version linear-utility-v1; the routing YAML version/checksum live in selected provenance.\" This means the database column `policy_version` is overloaded - it stores the scorer version, not the routing policy version. The routing policy version is only in the provenance JSONB. This could be confusing for queries and should be explicitly called out as a design decision. The migration 042 should document this.\n\n**Finding 9**: The openapi v1.1 `SelectModelRequest` has `task_signals` with `additionalProperties: true` (permissive for legacy) and `routing_profile` with `additionalProperties: false` (strict). But there's no validation that `routing_profile` is provided when the caller wants the new routing dimensions. The design says it's optional. This is fine.\n\n**Finding 10**: The spec.md says \"Config rules consume typed signals\" and \"the matching rule ID SHALL be recorded in decision provenance.\" The openapi `RoutingProvenance` has `matched_rule_ids` array. This is covered.\n\nLet me now formulate the findings with proper JSON format. This seems fine.\n\n3. **The routing-decision.schema.json has `source` with const \"coordinator\" and `success` with const true** - This means the audit event only represents successful coordinator decisions. The design says the RPC is atomic and only commits on success. Failed decisions don't create audit events (they return 503). Local fallback doesn't create audit events. This seems correct per design.\n\n4. **Work-packages.yaml wp-policy-service locks `agent-coordinator/src/vendor_registry.py` and `agent-coordinator/src/watchdog.py`** - These are dg-01 files. Since dg-04 depends on dg-01, modifying dg-01 files in dg-04 could be a coupling concern. But the design says the ConfiguredCatalogSync job goes in watchdog.py and the RoutingService uses VendorRegistryService in-process. The watchdog.py changes are for the new job. The vendor_registry.py might need changes to support the in-process usage pattern. This is a cross-cutting concern but may be acceptable.\n\n5. **The design D4 says \"The routing path constructs a read-only VendorRegistryService(audit=None)\"** - This creates a new instance without audit. The VendorRegistryService from dg-01 might not support audit=None parameter. This is an implementation detail but could be a compatibility issue.\n\n6. **The openapi v1.1 SelectModelRequest has `routing_profile` as optional with default null** - But the design says \"A new optional routing_profile is strict (extra=forbid)\". The schema has `additionalProperties: false` on TaskRoutingProfile, which is good. But the routing_profile itself is optional at the request level. This is fine for backward compatibility.\n\n7. **The work-packages.yaml wp-contract-config has `role: contracts-author` but no `archetype`** - Other packages have `archetype: implementer` or `archetype: validator`. This might be intentional since it's a contracts package.\n\n8. **The design D7 says \"The routing_decisions.policy_version column keeps dg-00 scorer version linear-utility-v1; the routing YAML version/checksum live in selected provenance.\"** - This means the database column policy_version is NOT updated to include routing policy version. The routing policy version/checksum is only in the provenance JSONB. This is a design decision that should be explicit. It could be a finding if it's not clearly communicated.\n\n9. **The tasks.md task 1.5 says \"Pin bounded persistence projection, typed exclusions, and exact local-fallback invariants in contracts.\"** - The contracts seem to cover this.\n\n10. **The spec.md says \"A periodic configuration-backed job SHALL materialize missing non-OpenRouter catalog identities from explicit lane metadata and the canonical provider model map without overwriting live catalog observations.\"** - This is the ConfiguredCatalogSync job. This seems covered.\n\n11. **The openapi v1.1 ExcludedAssignment reason pattern includes `cedar:` prefix** - This is a dg-00 reason. The design says \"DG-00's existing unavailable and quota:exhausted values remain accepted alongside DG-04's namespaced reasons.\" The pattern allows `(lane|policy|catalog|roadmap|registry|cedar):`. This seems correct.\n\n12. **The routing.yaml schema rule.when has minProperties: 1 but no required fields** - This means a rule could have just `phase` or just `scope`, etc. The design says \"Each rule has a typed when predicate over the profile and a typed constrain block\". This seems intentional for flexibility.\n\n13. **The work-packages.yaml wp-integration has `locks: {files: [], keys: [\"feature:task-routing:integration\"]}`** - Empty files lock but a key lock. This is fine for an integration package.\n\n14. **The design D3 says \"The Docker image copies the file beside agents.yaml and the loader resolves it from ROUTING_CONFIG or the package root, never the process working directory.\"** - This is good practice.\n\n15. **The spec.md requirement \"Honest local fallback\" says \"its catalog key SHALL be null because no live catalog join occurred\"** - The openapi RoutingProvenance has catalog_key as nullable array or null. The design D8 says \"The fallback table's order is only a deterministic choice among the lane's exact configured values\" - this implies all three dimensions. This is a spec_gap.\n\n**Finding 2**: The `routing-decision.schema.json` audit event has `source` with `const: \"coordinator\"` and `success` with `const: true`. This is a potential observability gap.\n\n**Finding 3**: The `wp-policy-service` package locks `agent-coordinator/src/vendor_registry.py` and `agent-coordinator/src/watchdog.py` which are dg-01 files. This is an implementation concern but the plan should specify that the loader is part of the contract. If dg-01's VendorRegistryService doesn't have this parameter, this is a breaking change to dg-01. This needs verification against dg-01's actual interface.\n\n**Finding 7**: The work-packages.yaml has `wp-contract-config` with `role: contracts-author` but no `archetype` field, while other packages have `archetype: implementer` or `archetype: validator`. The routing policy version is only in the provenance JSONB. This could be confusing for queries and should be explicitly called out as a design decision. This is fine.\n\n**Finding 10**: The spec.md says \"Config rules consume typed signals\" and \"the matching rule ID SHALL be recorded in decision provenance.\" The openapi `RoutingProvenance` has `matched_rule_ids` array. Missing or ambiguous projections remain explicit\nregistry misses and never become routable candidates.\n\n## D5 — Feasibility precedes DG-00 utility\n\nFor each exact lane/model pair, pure feasibility checks apply in deterministic order:\n\n1. live lane availability and lane/model rate limits;\n2. dispatchability, archetype, and requested/default dispatch mode;\n3. explicit/configured location and isolation constraints;\n4. roadmap-policy allow/exclude sets;\n5. catalog availability and dg-00 modality/quota constraints.\n\nReasons are machine-readable and sanitized. Those boundaries remain with\ndg-05, dg-06, and dg-07.\n\n## Dependencies\n\n- `dispatch-governance:dg-00` — model catalog, utility scorer, `/routing/*`, MCP mirror,\n  routing decision store, and exact static fallback equality.\n- `dispatch-governance:dg-01` — configured lane identity, typed location, live\n  availability/rate limits, and exact lane-to-catalog projections.\n\n## Acceptance Outcomes\n\n- `POST /routing/select_model` and `select_model_for_task` return location, isolation,\n  dispatch mode, and exact lane identity alongside the selected vendor/model.\n- Lane, task, and roadmap-policy feasibility is resolved before the existing dg-00\n  utility scorer runs; no second resolver or model call is introduced.\n- Every lane/model association comes from dg-01's exact catalog projection. Name\n  suffixes, publisher guesses, and fuzzy model matching are forbidden.\n- Changing validated `routing.yaml` rules changes deterministic decisions without code\n  edits, and the policy version/checksum is recorded.\n- Coordinator-side decisions are durably recorded in both routing decision storage and\n  coordinator audit. Local fallback decisions declare that durable audit was unavailable.\n- The dg-00 fallback contract remains byte-for-byte equal for existing\n  `resolve_archetype_for_phase` callers when adaptive routing is disabled, fails, or\n  times out.\n\n## Non-goals\n\n- No `/route/task` endpoint or parallel scoring implementation.\n- No per-dispatch-mode isolation override or precedence ladder (dg-05).\n- No orchestrator call-site wiring, redispatch, or loop-control changes (dg-06).\n- No operating-system isolation enforcement (dg-07).\n- No duplicate price table, roster, health cache, or inferred vendor identity.\n"}],"isError":false,"timestamp":1789599353633}}

openspec/changes/implement-the-task-router-vendor-x-location-x-model/reviews/raw-pi-plan.txt:137:{"type":"message_start","message":{"role":"toolResult","toolCallId":"chatcmpl-tool-6fa4d43067ca41349e99b62304c9ddaa","toolName":"read","content":[{"type":"text","text":"# Design: extend routing to vendor × location × isolation × dispatch mode\n\n## D1 — Extend one resolver and one public operation\n\nDG-04 extends the dg-00 `RoutingService.select_model()` pipeline, HTTP\n`POST /routing/select_model`, and MCP `select_model_for_task`. It does not add\n`POST /route/task`, a second score function, or a second routing decision store.\nThe existing `selected.vendor/model/endpoint_kind` meaning remains observable and\nunchanged; assignment and provenance are additive fields.\n\n## D2 — Preserve compatibility with an optional strict profile\n\nLegacy `task_signals` remains accepted with its current permissive extra-field\nbehavior because existing phase callers send fields such as `write_allow`. A new\noptional `routing_profile` is strict (`extra=forbid`) and types:\n\n- expected duration seconds;\n- scope category (`read-only|bounded-write|broad-write`);\n- interactivity (`interactive|headless`);\n- secret need category (`none|brokered|direct`), never a secret value;\n- positive parallelism;\n- repository shape (`single-package|monorepo|unknown`);\n- roadmap-policy constraints (allowed/excluded lane/vendor/location sets);\n- optional required location, isolation, and dispatch mode.\n\nPydantic validates the external boundary and FastAPI/MCP share the same request model.\nNew response objects are optional-with-default for legacy validation but are always\npopulated by a successful DG-04 service decision.\n\n## D3 — Rules are ordered, typed, and versioned\n\n`agent-coordinator/routing.yaml` carries `schema_version`, `policy_version`,\nphase defaults, ordered first-match rules, and a fallback-dimension table. A dedicated\nloader validates unknown fields, duplicate IDs, enum values, ranges, and phase defaults,\nthen records a SHA-256 checksum of canonical file bytes.\n\nEach rule has a typed `when` predicate over the profile and a typed `set` block for\nlocation, isolation, and dispatch mode. Explicit request constraints take precedence;\notherwise the first matching rule supplies a dimension and phase/default values fill the\nremainder. Rules narrow feasibility and never add a second utility score. Changing a\nrule therefore changes the feasible assignment set without code edits.\n\nThe Docker image copies the file beside `agents.yaml` and the loader resolves it from\n`ROUTING_CONFIG` or the package root, never the process working directory.\n\n## D4 — DG-01 is the only lane source and joins are exact\n\n`RoutingService` injects/loads `VendorRegistryService` in process and requests all\nlanes without `available_only` prefiltering so exclusion provenance is retained. For\neach lane it consumes dg-01's projected catalog models. It forms an assignment only when\nthe catalog candidate identity exactly equals the projection key:\n\n`(catalog_vendor, model, endpoint_kind, base_url)`.\n\n`base_url` and additive lane identity travel through `CandidateInput` and\n`ScoredCandidate`. Agent-name suffixes, provider/publisher guesses, substring matches,\nand fuzzy model names are forbidden. Missing or ambiguous projections remain explicit\nregistry misses and never become routable candidates.\n\n## D5 — Feasibility precedes DG-00 utility\n\nFor each exact lane/model pair, pure feasibility checks apply in deterministic order:\n\n1. live lane availability and lane/model rate limits;\n2. dispatchability, archetype, and requested/default dispatch mode;\n3. explicit/configured location and isolation constraints;\n4. roadmap-policy allow/exclude sets;\n5. catalog availability and dg-00 modality/quota constraints.\n\nReasons are machine-readable and sanitized. Only feasible lane/model candidates enter\nthe existing `score_and_rank`; DG-04 does not duplicate quality, posterior, cost,\nlatency, headroom, or exploration math. Multiple lanes may project the same catalog\nmodel, so the final stable order is `(-score, agent_id, catalog identity)`.\n\n## D6 — Assignment and provenance are additive\n\nA successful response adds top-level:\n\n- `assignment`: exact `agent_id`, `vendor_type`, `policy_vendor`,\n  `catalog_vendor`, location, isolation, dispatch mode, model, endpoint kind, and base\n  URL;\n- `provenance`: source (`coordinator` or `local-static`), policy version/checksum,\n  matched rule IDs, rationale, persistence flag, durable-audit flag, and exact\n  lane/catalog key.\n\nAlternatives retain their own lane assignment rather than losing identity after model\nscoring. Existing selected-candidate fields remain intact for older consumers.\n\n## D7 — Durable routing record is authoritative; audit event is linked\n\nThe existing `routing_decisions` row is the authoritative durable routing audit. Its\nJSONB request/selected/alternatives/excluded fields accept additive assignment and\nprovenance, so no schema migration is required.\n\nAfter that row is inserted, DG-04 emits a sanitized `routing_decision` audit-log event\nthat links only the decision ID, selected agent/model, policy version, and source. The\nwrite uses an awaited durable audit operation and fails the request if durability cannot\nbe established; fire-and-forget acceptance is insufficient. The generic audit event is\nan index/link, not a second source of routing truth.\n\nNo raw secret, environment value, prompt, or unbounded path list enters either record;\nonly typed secret-need and scope categories are retained.\n\n## D8 — Local fallback is configuration-derived and honest\n\nA skills-side bridge/helper may fall back only after transport timeout/unreachability. It\nloads the checkout's validated `routing.yaml`, `agents.yaml`, and archetype model map,\nthen combines the caller's already-resolved static provider/model with the fallback\ndimension order. It never embeds a roster, fabricates availability, or performs fuzzy\nassociation.\n\nThe response has the normal assignment shape plus `fallback=true`,\n`source=local-static`, `persisted=false`, `durable_audit=false`, and a bounded\nfailure reason. A local UUID is explicitly not retrievable from coordinator decision\nstorage.\n\nThe existing `resolve_archetype_for_phase` fallback is not rewritten: disabled,\nfailure, malformed-response, and timeout paths still return the exact dg-00 static\n`ResolvedArchetype` object with no added reasons or fields.\n\n## D9 — DG-05/DG-06 boundaries remain closed\n\nDG-04 carries the lane's current configured isolation as data and may filter an explicit\nrequest. It does not define per-mode overrides, the isolation precedence ladder, or\nenforcement; DG-05 owns that contract. It does not call routing before `dispatch_fn`,\nchange `phase_agent.py`, redispatch work, or add loop caps; DG-06 owns obedience.\nNo sandbox is launched; DG-07 owns enforcement.\n\n## D10 — Test-first packages and validation\n\nContract/config tests fail first, followed by pure policy/association tests, then service\nand transport/fallback tests. PostgreSQL coverage proves the additive JSONB decision\nround trip and durable audit link. Full coordinator and affected skills suites, Ruff,\nstrict mypy, strict OpenSpec, work-package DAG/scope checks, configured vendor-panel\nplan/implementation convergence, stacked PR CI, and exact static-fallback regression\nmust all pass before roadmap reconciliation.\n\nFramework-specific implementation follows the installed FastAPI/Pydantic versions and\ntheir official model/response documentation:\nhttps://docs.pydantic.dev/latest/concepts/models/ and\nhttps://fastapi.tiangolo.com/tutorial/response-model/.\n"}],"isError":false,"timestamp":1789599353633}}
