     1	# Add Dispatch Sandbox Enforcement
     2	
     3	> Parent roadmap: `dispatch-governance` (`dg-07`)
     4	> Change ID: `add-dispatch-sandbox-enforcement`
     5	> Prerequisites: dg-02, dg-03, dg-05, and dg-06 are landed
     6	
     7	## Why
     8	
     9	The router now chooses an isolation posture and the orchestrator carries that immutable
    10	decision to execution, but local vendor CLI processes still run with the host user's OS
    11	authority. A `worktree` prevents concurrent agents from sharing one checkout; it does not
    12	prevent reads outside that checkout, writes elsewhere, or arbitrary egress. The coordinator's
    13	network policy is likewise advisory because it is checked only by callers that volunteer a
    14	domain.
    15	
    16	dg-07 closes the local execution gap. A shared local-process backend consumes the exact dg-06
    17	decision, renders the coordinator's policy for Anthropic Sandbox Runtime (SRT), and applies the
    18	result to every vendor CLI lifecycle command: synchronous invocation, asynchronous submission,
    19	polling, and the autopilot local-provider harness.
    20	
    21	## What Changes
    22	
    23	### Immutable execution context
    24	
    25	Dispatch receives a versioned execution context containing the routing decision identifier,
    26	exact agent/lane identifier, isolation, dispatch mode, canonical worktree root, and provenance.
    27	The enforcement layer never re-runs routing. Standalone review-panel calls that have no routed
    28	context resolve the already-landed dg-05 fallback once from the exact `agents.yaml` lane.
    29	Routed callers carry the complete context in phase payload v2; every adapter lifecycle method
    30	accepts that context explicitly instead of reconstructing it from cwd.
    31	
    32	### Coordinator-owned network-policy export and audit
    33	
    34	`NetworkPolicyService` gains an exact-agent export. It returns the active profile-specific and
    35	global rules, a closed default-deny contract, schema revision, and a deterministic digest.
    36	Rendering is conservative: SRT denies take precedence, so conflicting authored rules may become
    37	narrower but never wider. A malformed or unavailable cold-start export renders deny-all; it does
    38	not invent destinations.
    39	
    40	A narrow sandbox-execution audit endpoint durably and idempotently records applied and degraded
    41	outcomes. If the coordinator is unavailable, a locked mode-0600 JSONL outbox under the operator's
    42	XDG state directory is fsynced and retried oldest-first on later calls. An unsandboxed fallback is
    43	allowed only after either the coordinator event or the durable outbox record succeeds.
    44	
    45	### Pure renderer and lifecycle-owning backend
    46	
    47	`skills/shared/sandbox_profile.py` provides:
    48	
    49	- pure, deterministic SRT settings rendering;
    50	- mode-aware filesystem policy (`review` has no project write roots; write-capable modes are
    51	  confined to the canonical worktree root; every lane gets an ephemeral vendor-state root);
    52	- a prepared-command lifecycle that owns a unique mode-0600 settings file, sanitized environment,
    53	  runtime identity, policy digest, process group, and cleanup;
    54	- an additive renderer seam for future runtimes.
    55	
    56	The reviewed runtime is `@anthropic-ai/sandbox-runtime` 0.0.77 on Node >=20.11.0. The repository
    57	pins the package and integrity and never installs it during dispatch. Setup/CI install the pin;
    58	runtime discovery is explicit absolute override, then the dispatcher's Git-root installation,
    59	then unavailable. The runtime is accepted only when package metadata and integrity match. On Linux
    60	the preflight also verifies `bubblewrap`, `socat`,
    61	`ripgrep`, user-namespace capability, architecture/seccomp support, and a real no-op SRT launch.
    62	
    63	Official runtime sources:
    64	
    65	- https://github.com/anthropics/sandbox-runtime
    66	- https://github.com/anthropics/sandbox-runtime/blob/main/README.md
    67	- https://github.com/anthropics/sandbox-runtime/blob/main/package.json
    68	- https://github.com/anthropics/sandbox-runtime/security/advisories/GHSA-9gqj-5w7c-vx47
    69	
    70	### One local command backend
    71	
    72	The shared backend replaces direct vendor subprocess launches in `CliVendorAdapter` sync submit,
    73	async submit and poll paths, and in `autopilot/scripts/provider_dispatch.py`. Poll enforcement
    74	failures are collection failures retried to the existing deadline, not terminal remote-task
    75	failures. A structural guard
    76	prevents future vendor CLI subprocess sinks outside the backend. Non-sandbox decisions preserve
    77	argv, stdin, cwd, timeout, and result behavior.
    78	
    79	### Loud, bounded degradation
    80	
    81	Fail-open is restricted to facts known before a vendor process starts: unsupported OS, missing or
    82	incompatible pinned runtime, or failed platform capability preflight. Those cases warn, durably
    83	audit `applied=false`, and run the original command. Unsafe roots, malformed policy, settings
    84	materialization errors, and audit/outbox failures fail closed. Once SRT starts, a timeout or
    85	unknown failure never triggers an unsandboxed retry because doing so could execute work twice.
    86	
    87	## Scope Boundary
    88	
    89	This change protects against accidental or confused local tool behavior after sandbox startup.
    90	It does not claim containment of a malicious vendor executable, a compromised runtime, same-user
    91	races, damage inside an authorized writable root, or exfiltration through an allowed destination
    92	such as GitHub. It strips proxy and code-injection environment variables required to preserve the
    93	SRT boundary, but vendor credentials deliberately supplied to a CLI remain readable by that CLI.
    94	Request-time secret substitution is dg-08; broader credential brokering and cloud execution remain
    95	owned by `add-sandboxed-harness-execution`.
    96	
    97	dg-03's factual `posture.filesystem` means a per-session workspace exists; it is not a security
    98	attestation and never satisfies a router request for `sandbox`. Wrapping a local submission CLI
    99	also does not imply that a remote worker is sandboxed.
   100	
   101	## Approaches Considered
   102	
   103	### Shared SRT local-process backend (selected)
   104	
   105	One policy renderer and one lifecycle-owning runner cover every current local CLI sink. It enforces
   106	the already-authored isolation and network decisions without creating a second router.
   107	
   108	### Vendor-native flags only
   109	
   110	Rejected. Vendor flags differ, omit network enforcement, and leave vendors without a native
   111	sandbox unprotected.
   112	
   113	### Coordinator-managed containers
   114	
   115	Deferred. A container/control-plane backend belongs to the downstream sandboxed-harness change;
   116	dg-07 supplies the local backend and renderer seam it consumes.
   117	
   118	## Impact
   119	
   120	- New shared runtime: `skills/shared/sandbox_profile.py` and local process backend helpers.
   121	- Modified execution sinks: review dispatcher and autopilot local-provider dispatch.
   122	- Modified coordinator: exact-agent policy export and durable sandbox audit endpoint.
   123	- Modified config projection: effective per-mode isolation reaches standalone adapters.
   124	- New pinned optional tool dependency: SRT 0.0.77.
   125	- New contracts, tests, operational documentation, and real-runtime probes.
   126	- New capable-host GitHub Actions evidence gate, with a recorded configured-vendor CLI pass.
   127	
   128	## Rollback
   129	
   130	Removing a mode's `sandbox` decision restores the byte-compatible local process path. Removing or
   131	breaking the runtime does not silently claim enforcement: the preflight records a durable degraded
   132	event before the legacy command may run.
     1	# Design: Dispatch sandbox enforcement
     2	
     3	## Context
     4	
     5	dg-02 supplies structured vendor results, dg-03 supplies factual environment posture, dg-05
     6	pins isolation vocabulary and fallback, and dg-06 carries one immutable routing decision. dg-07
     7	is the execution consumer. The current two subprocess call families are the multi-vendor review
     8	dispatcher and autopilot's local Pi provider.
     9	
    10	## Decisions
    11	
    12	### D1 — Consume one immutable execution context
    13	
    14	`DispatchExecutionContext` carries the exact agent id, dispatch mode, isolation, decision id,
    15	provenance, location, enforcement scope, and canonical root. The roadmap host constructs it at
    16	the dispatch boundary from dg-06's validated assignment plus the managed worktree root and passes
    17	it through `PhaseDispatchPayload.execution_context`. `CliVendorAdapter.dispatch()`,
    18	`dispatch_async()`, and `poll_for_result()` receive the same explicit context. Standalone panel
    19	callers construct one context at their adapter boundary from the exact lane's mode override, then
    20	entry value, and the invocation cwd validated through `checkout_policy.py`. A router-sourced
    21	context requires a non-null decision id. No renderer or backend calls routing or derives a root
    22	from ambient process cwd.
    23	
    24	Context producers are explicit:
    25	
    26	| Caller | Assignment fields | Execution root |
    27	| --- | --- | --- |
    28	| Routed roadmap/autopilot phase | Copy decision id, agent, isolation, location, and mode from the persisted dg-06 decision into payload v2 | Host adds the validated managed-worktree root |
    29	| Standalone vendor panel | Resolve exact-lane mode override, then entry isolation, exactly once | Adapter validates its explicit invocation cwd |
    30	| Autopilot local provider | Consume payload v2 unchanged; no legacy reconstruction | Required in the embedded context |
    31	
    32	dg-03 posture is diagnostic evidence only. Its filesystem bit means a per-session workspace, not
    33	credential containment; its network bit does not prove equivalence to the active coordinator
    34	policy. Neither bit satisfies `isolation=sandbox`.
    35	
    36	### D2 — One local process backend, not one list wrapper
    37	
    38	All vendor CLI execution sites call `skills/shared/local_process_backend.py`. The pure renderer in
    39	`sandbox_profile.py` returns settings and a digest; an impure prepared-command context manager
    40	validates runtime/root/policy and materializes a unique 0600 file. The backend constructs argv and
    41	environment and owns process-group termination and cleanup. `build_command()` remains pure and
    42	vendor-specific.
    43	
    44	The argv is `[absolute_srt, "--settings", settings_path, "--", absolute_vendor, ...]` as
    45	documented by SRT. Options that weaken nested, network, Unix-socket, local-binding, or Apple Event
    46	isolation are never project-configurable.
    47	
    48	### D3 — Mode-aware filesystem policy
    49	
    50	Review and validation-shaped commands receive no project write roots. Alternative, quick,
    51	implementation, and documentation-shaped commands may write only the strict canonical worktree
    52	root. Every sandboxed command receives a backend-owned, per-launch state root used for HOME,
    53	XDG state/config/cache, and runtime temporary files, so vendor CLIs do not need write access to
    54	the operator's home. Read-only credential inputs and required environment credential keys remain
    55	explicit per-vendor configuration; no renderer hard-codes them. The root must exist, equal `git
    56	rev-parse --show-toplevel`, pass the existing `checkout_policy.py` managed-worktree check, and
    57	must not be `/`, the user's home, or the shared checkout.
    58	
    59	The worktree `.git` pointer and linked-worktree common Git metadata are explicitly denied for
    60	writes. A sandboxed worker may edit files but skill prompts do not ask it to commit; the host
    61	orchestrator validates and creates the save-point commit after collecting the worker result. This
    62	avoids granting one agent write access to shared objects and refs.
    63	Symlink escapes are rejected/tested; hardlink aliasing is measured and documented as a residual
    64	same-user risk rather than overstated as contained.
    65	
    66	### D4 — Exact-agent, default-deny network export
    67	
    68	The coordinator exports a snapshot from the exact agent's profile assignment plus global rules.
    69	The snapshot uses a closed SRT-compatible hostname plus separately range-checked port grammar,
    70	explicit scope and priority, schema revision, and canonical SHA-256 digest. Migration 044 adds
    71	`updated_at` and an atomic exact-agent export function; `policy_revision` is the maximum included
    72	row update timestamp plus row count, while the digest is the canonical content change detector.
    73	Disabled rules are absent.
    74	
    75	SRT's deny-first semantics cannot represent every ordered SQL policy exactly. Rendering therefore
    76	keeps every applicable deny and only authored allows; conflicts become narrower. New writes are
    77	validated against the export grammar. Any legacy malformed applicable rule makes the entire export
    78	unrenderable and therefore deny-all; rules are never silently omitted. An unavailable snapshot
    79	becomes deny-all. A default-allow snapshot is not renderable by this backend and fails closed. The
    80	export contract is authoritative for sandbox execution; the older advisory SQL matcher is not used
    81	to construct SRT settings.
    82	
    83	Provider endpoints are not hard-coded in the renderer. Current seed policy lacks several vendor
    84	API domains, so dg-07 does not flip existing local lanes to `sandbox`; rollout requires an
    85	authored endpoint inventory and a successful preflight. The controlled acceptance CLI exercises
    86	enforcement independently of production vendor endpoints.
    87	
    88	The autopilot `local` provider is rollout-ineligible under `sandbox` until its authored hostname
    89	and port are exportable and SRT supports the destination class. Loopback, link-local, private-IP,
    90	or mDNS rejection is a fail-closed policy/capability outcome, never a fail-open reason.
    91	
    92	### D5 — Sanitize boundary-shaping environment, do not claim secret brokering
    93	
    94	The environment passed to SRT itself and inherited by its child removes inherited proxy variables,
    95	loader/startup injection variables, Git path/config overrides, and untrusted temp settings that
    96	can alter SRT or its child. This prevents an ambient parent proxy from bypassing SRT address
    97	checks. The unsandboxed compatibility path retains the caller's original environment byte for
    98	byte. Runtime discovery records absolute Node, SRT entrypoint, `bwrap`, `socat`, and `rg` paths and
    99	constructs a minimal trusted PATH from their parent directories; vendor executables are absolute
   100	and inherited descriptors are closed. Remaining required vendor
   101	credentials are still readable by the vendor process; dg-08 owns request-time substitution and
   102	the downstream sandboxed-harness change owns broader credential brokering.
   103	
   104	### D6 — Narrow fail-open with durable evidence
   105	
   106	Only unsupported OS, missing/incompatible pinned runtime, or failed pre-launch capability probe
   107	may run the original command. The backend first writes a durable coordinator event; if unavailable,
   108	it appends and fsyncs JSONL under
   109	`${XDG_STATE_HOME:-~/.local/state}/agentic-coding-tools/sandbox-events/outbox.jsonl`, with a 0700
   110	parent, 0600 file, advisory lock, and directory fsync. The path is outside every checkout and is
   111	never exposed as sandbox-writable. Failure of both blocks dispatch. Unsafe root,
   112	unrenderable policy, materialization failure, and all post-SRT-start failures fail closed.
   113	
   114	Each later event attempt drains older outbox entries before writing the new one, removing a record
   115	only after the endpoint acknowledges its `event_id`. Migration 044 makes `event_id` unique; replay
   116	returns the original durable audit row id. Audit payloads
   117	contain key names and digests, never prompt/argv bodies, settings bodies, or secret values.
   118	
   119	### D7 — Pin and probe SRT
   120	
   121	The repository pins `@anthropic-ai/sandbox-runtime` 0.0.77 with lockfile integrity and Node
   122	>=20.11.0. `install.sh` and CI may run `npm ci` in `tools/sandbox-runtime`; dispatch performs no
   123	installation. Discovery order is an explicit absolute override, then the dispatcher's own Git
   124	top-level `tools/sandbox-runtime` installation, then unavailable. Runtime copies never resolve
   125	relative to `__file__`. The backend launches the absolute Node binary and pinned absolute SRT JS
   126	entrypoint only after package version and lockfile integrity metadata match. Versions before
   127	0.0.16 are forbidden by the official network-escape advisory.
   128	
   129	Linux preflight checks `bwrap`, `socat`, `rg`, supported architecture/seccomp conditions,
   130	user-namespace/AppArmor viability, and a no-op sandbox launch. macOS checks the supported native
   131	backend and a no-op launch. This host currently lacks `socat` and restricts unprivileged user
   132	namespaces, so real enforcement evidence must run on a capable host; local tests must report the
   133	skip reason, never manufacture a pass.
   134	
   135	Sources:
   136	
   137	- https://github.com/anthropics/sandbox-runtime/blob/main/README.md
   138	- https://github.com/anthropics/sandbox-runtime/blob/main/package.json
   139	- https://github.com/anthropics/sandbox-runtime/security/advisories/GHSA-9gqj-5w7c-vx47
   140	
   141	### D8 — Backend coverage and timeout ownership
   142	
   143	Sync submit, async submit, poll, repair retry, snapshot fallback, and autopilot local-provider
   144	launch all use the backend exactly once per process attempt. There is no cancellation subprocess
   145	today; any future configured cancellation command is covered by the same structural guard. The
   146	actual invocation cwd is the policy root. A pre-launch enforcement denial during polling is a
   147	retryable collection condition until the existing poll deadline; it must not close a still-running
   148	remote task as a vendor failure. On timeout the backend starts a new session, sends TERM to the
   149	process group, waits a bounded grace period, sends KILL if required, waits, and then cleans owned
   150	material. It never replays unsandboxed after process start.
   151	
   152	### D9 — Ownership relative to sandboxed-harness execution
   153	
   154	dg-07 owns the local process seam, local SRT backend, network export, and sandbox execution audit.
   155	`add-sandboxed-harness-execution` consumes them and retains cloud backends, credential brokering,
   156	and trust-gate coupling. Its duplicate local-backend/export task groups are reconciled after dg-07
   157	lands.
   158	
   159	## Validation strategy
   160	
   161	Tests begin RED at each contract boundary. Unit and integration tests cover decision immutability,
   162	policy normalization, deterministic rendering, root validation, environment stripping, hostile
   163	argv, durable degradation, cleanup, and every subprocess sink. A static AST guard prevents new
   164	vendor process launches outside the backend.
   165	
   166	A capability-gated real-runtime test must demonstrate read/write and egress restrictions on a
   167	supported Ubuntu or macOS runner and run at least one configured real vendor executable through
   168	the same backend. A manually dispatched GitHub Actions workflow uses `macos-14` as the canonical
   169	capable runner and uploads `sandbox-runtime-evidence.json`; the checked-in completion record lives
   170	at `openspec/changes/add-dispatch-sandbox-enforcement/evidence/sandbox-runtime-evidence.json` and
   171	includes workflow/run identity. The gate reports `unsupported` with exact prerequisites on an
   172	incapable host; roadmap completion requires at least one recorded capable-host pass.
   173	
   174	## Residual risks
   175	
   176	- A permitted destination such as GitHub remains an exfiltration channel.
   177	- A child can read credentials intentionally supplied to it.
   178	- Hardlinks and same-user races may exceed path-only containment.
   179	- SRT is pre-1.0 and its config may change; the exact pin and renderer tests bound that risk.

     1	## ADDED Requirements
     2	
     3	### Requirement: Local vendor CLI execution SHALL use one enforcement backend
     4	
     5	Every local vendor CLI lifecycle command SHALL pass through one shared process backend. This
     6	includes synchronous execution, asynchronous submission, asynchronous polling, and the autopilot
     7	local-provider harness. Discovery and health probes are control-plane operations and are explicitly
     8	excluded. No cancellation subprocess exists today; any future configured vendor cancellation
     9	command SHALL use the same backend.
    10	
    11	#### Scenario: Every vendor lifecycle command uses the backend
    12	
    13	WHEN a configured local vendor CLI is submitted, polled, or run synchronously
    14	THEN exactly one shared backend invocation SHALL own process creation
    15	AND a structural guard SHALL reject new direct vendor subprocess sinks.
    16	
    17	#### Scenario: Non-sandbox behavior remains compatible
    18	
    19	WHEN effective isolation is `none` or `worktree`
    20	THEN the backend SHALL preserve argv, stdin, cwd, timeout, and result behavior
    21	AND no sandbox settings file SHALL be created.
    22	
    23	### Requirement: Enforcement SHALL consume the immutable routing decision
    24	
    25	The backend SHALL consume the dg-06 routing decision attached to dispatch context and SHALL NOT
    26	call routing again. A standalone caller without routed context SHALL resolve dg-05's exact-lane
    27	fallback once at the adapter boundary and record that provenance.
    28	
    29	#### Scenario: Routed execution is not re-resolved
    30	
    31	WHEN dispatch context carries a validated routing decision and isolation assignment
    32	THEN the same decision identifier and assignment SHALL appear in the execution audit
    33	AND no router request SHALL occur during rendering, preparation, or process execution.
    34	
    35	#### Scenario: Standalone dispatch resolves the exact lane
    36	
    37	WHEN a review-panel dispatch has no routed context
    38	THEN effective isolation SHALL be resolved from its exact agent id and dispatch mode
    39	AND an entry-level value SHALL be inherited only when that mode has no override.
    40	
    41	### Requirement: Sandbox rendering SHALL be pure and mode-aware
    42	
    43	The SRT renderer SHALL be deterministic and side-effect free. Review mode SHALL receive no project
    44	worktree write access. Write-capable modes MAY write only beneath a strictly resolved canonical Git
    45	worktree root. Per-launch vendor state SHALL be isolated from the operator's home. Reads of named
    46	credential locations SHALL be denied except for explicit per-vendor credential inputs pending
    47	dg-08.
    48	
    49	#### Scenario: Review is read-only
    50	
    51	WHEN a `sandbox` decision is rendered for review
    52	THEN `filesystem.allowWrite` SHALL contain no project path
    53	AND an attempted project write inside or outside the worktree SHALL fail
    54	AND only the backend-owned ephemeral state root and SRT's documented internal paths MAY remain
    55	writable.
    56	
    57	#### Scenario: Write-capable work is root-confined
    58	
    59	WHEN a `sandbox` decision is rendered for an alternative or quick dispatch
    60	THEN the only project write root SHALL be the canonical worktree root
    61	AND the worktree `.git` pointer and common Git metadata SHALL be denied for writes
    62	AND writes through path or symlink escapes SHALL fail.
    63	
    64	#### Scenario: Rendering has no effects
    65	
    66	WHEN identical validated context and policy inputs are rendered twice
    67	THEN the policy documents and digests SHALL be identical
    68	AND rendering SHALL NOT write files, spawn processes, or contact a service.
    69	
    70	### Requirement: Prepared sandbox commands SHALL own lifecycle and truthful state
    71	
    72	The impure preparation layer SHALL own a unique mode-0600 settings file, sanitized child
    73	environment, absolute executable paths, process group, applied/degraded metadata, and cleanup.
    74	The wrapped argv SHALL separate SRT options from the vendor argv with `--`.
    75	
    76	#### Scenario: Concurrent launches do not share policy material
    77	
    78	WHEN two sandboxed commands are prepared concurrently
    79	THEN each SHALL receive a distinct settings path
    80	AND success, failure, and timeout SHALL remove only that command's material.
    81	
    82	#### Scenario: Timeout terminates the complete process tree
    83	
    84	WHEN a sandboxed vendor command exceeds its timeout
    85	THEN the backend SHALL terminate its process group, wait, escalate if required, and clean up
    86	AND no child process, listener, settings file, or owned mount artifact SHALL remain.
    87	
    88	#### Scenario: Execution metadata is truthful
    89	
    90	WHEN a sandbox was requested but not applied
    91	THEN result and audit metadata SHALL report `requested=sandbox` and `applied=false`
    92	AND the dispatch SHALL NOT describe itself as sandboxed.
    93	
    94	### Requirement: Degradation SHALL be narrow, durable, and pre-launch
    95	
    96	Unsandboxed fallback SHALL occur only for a preflight-proven unsupported platform, absent or
    97	incompatible pinned runtime, or failed platform capability probe. A warning and durable audit or
    98	outbox event SHALL exist before launch. Unsafe roots, malformed policies, and audit persistence
    99	failure SHALL fail closed. No post-launch sandbox failure SHALL be retried unsandboxed.
   100	
   101	#### Scenario: Missing runtime degrades visibly
   102	
   103	WHEN isolation is `sandbox` and the pinned runtime is absent
   104	THEN a durable `applied=false` event SHALL be recorded before the original command starts
   105	AND the command MAY proceed unsandboxed with a warning.
   106	
   107	#### Scenario: Audit failure blocks fail-open
   108	
   109	WHEN neither coordinator audit persistence nor the local durable outbox succeeds
   110	THEN the unsandboxed vendor command SHALL NOT start.
   111	
   112	#### Scenario: Poll enforcement failure does not abandon remote work
   113	
   114	WHEN an asynchronous poll is blocked before its vendor process starts by sandbox enforcement
   115	THEN the collector SHALL retain the remote task and retry until its existing deadline
   116	AND SHALL NOT classify the remote vendor task itself as failed.
   117	
   118	#### Scenario: Runtime failure never duplicates work
   119	
   120	WHEN SRT has started and exits nonzero or times out
   121	THEN the backend SHALL return that failure
   122	AND SHALL NOT retry the vendor command without the sandbox.
   123	
   124	### Requirement: The runtime dependency SHALL be pinned and probed
   125	
   126	The supported SRT package version and integrity SHALL be committed. Dispatch SHALL never install a
   127	runtime. Runtime selection SHALL validate package metadata, Node's version floor, platform
   128	dependencies, and a no-op launch before reporting `applied=true`.
   129	
   130	#### Scenario: Incompatible runtime is not trusted
   131	
   132	WHEN an executable named `srt` is present but its package metadata does not match the pin
   133	THEN the preflight SHALL classify it as incompatible
   134	AND degradation SHALL follow the durable pre-launch path.
   135	
   136	#### Scenario: Known network-escape versions are rejected
   137	
   138	WHEN the detected package version is older than 0.0.16
   139	THEN it SHALL never be used for network enforcement.

     1	"""Network access policy service for Agent Coordinator.
     2	
     3	Provides domain-level access control for agent network requests.
     4	Policies are per-profile with global fallbacks.
     5	"""
     6	
     7	from dataclasses import dataclass
     8	from typing import Any
     9	
    10	from .config import get_config
    11	from .db import DatabaseClient, get_db
    12	
    13	
    14	@dataclass
    15	class AccessDecision:
    16	    """Result of a domain access check."""
    17	
    18	    allowed: bool
    19	    domain: str
    20	    reason: str | None = None
    21	    policy_id: str | None = None
    22	
    23	    @classmethod
    24	    def from_dict(cls, data: dict[str, Any]) -> "AccessDecision":
    25	        return cls(
    26	            allowed=data.get("allowed", False),
    27	            domain=data.get("domain", ""),
    28	            reason=data.get("reason"),
    29	            policy_id=str(data["policy_id"]) if data.get("policy_id") else None,
    30	        )
    31	
    32	
    33	class NetworkPolicyService:
    34	    """Service for network access policy enforcement."""
    35	
    36	    def __init__(self, db: DatabaseClient | None = None):
    37	        self._db = db
    38	
    39	    @property
    40	    def db(self) -> DatabaseClient:
    41	        if self._db is None:
    42	            self._db = get_db()
    43	        return self._db
    44	
    45	    async def check_domain(
    46	        self,
    47	        domain: str,
    48	        agent_id: str | None = None,
    49	    ) -> AccessDecision:
    50	        """Check if an agent is allowed to access a domain.
    51	
    52	        Args:
    53	            domain: The domain to check (e.g., 'github.com')
    54	            agent_id: Agent making the request (default: from config)
    55	
    56	        Returns:
    57	            AccessDecision with allowed status and reason
    58	        """
    59	        config = get_config()
    60	        agent_id = agent_id or config.agent.agent_id
    61	
    62	        try:
    63	            result = await self.db.rpc(
    64	                "is_domain_allowed",
    65	                {
    66	                    "p_agent_id": agent_id,
    67	                    "p_domain": domain,
    68	                },
    69	            )
    70	            return AccessDecision.from_dict(result)
    71	        except Exception:
    72	            # On error, apply default policy
    73	            default_allowed = config.network_policy.default_policy == "allow"
    74	            return AccessDecision(
    75	                allowed=default_allowed,
    76	                domain=domain,
    77	                reason=f"default_policy:{config.network_policy.default_policy}",
    78	            )
    79	
    80	
    81	# Global service instance
    82	_network_policy_service: NetworkPolicyService | None = None
    83	
    84	
    85	def get_network_policy_service() -> NetworkPolicyService:
    86	    """Get the global network policy service instance."""
    87	    global _network_policy_service
    88	    if _network_policy_service is None:
    89	        _network_policy_service = NetworkPolicyService()
    90	    return _network_policy_service
     1	"""Audit trail service for Agent Coordinator.
     2	
     3	Provides immutable, async logging of all coordination operations.
     4	Audit entries are append-only — the database enforces immutability via triggers.
     5	"""
     6	
     7	import asyncio
     8	import logging
     9	import time
    10	from dataclasses import dataclass, field
    11	from datetime import datetime
    12	from typing import Any
    13	
    14	from .config import get_config
    15	from .db import DatabaseClient, get_db
    16	
    17	logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
    18	
    19	
    20	@dataclass
    21	class AuditEntry:
    22	    """Represents an audit log entry."""
    23	
    24	    id: str
    25	    agent_id: str
    26	    agent_type: str | None
    27	    operation: str
    28	    parameters: dict[str, Any] = field(default_factory=dict)
    29	    result: dict[str, Any] = field(default_factory=dict)
    30	    duration_ms: int | None = None
    31	    success: bool | None = None
    32	    error_message: str | None = None
    33	    created_at: datetime | None = None
    34	    delegated_from: str | None = None
    35	
    36	    @classmethod
    37	    def from_dict(cls, data: dict[str, Any]) -> "AuditEntry":
    38	        created_at = None
    39	        if data.get("created_at"):
    40	            created_at = datetime.fromisoformat(
    41	                str(data["created_at"]).replace("Z", "+00:00")
    42	            )
    43	        return cls(
    44	            id=str(data["id"]),
    45	            agent_id=data["agent_id"],
    46	            agent_type=data.get("agent_type"),
    47	            operation=data["operation"],
    48	            parameters=data.get("parameters") or {},
    49	            result=data.get("result") or {},
    50	            duration_ms=data.get("duration_ms"),
    51	            success=data.get("success"),
    52	            error_message=data.get("error_message"),
    53	            created_at=created_at,
    54	            delegated_from=data.get("delegated_from"),
    55	        )
    56	
    57	
    58	@dataclass
    59	class AuditResult:
    60	    """Result of an audit logging operation."""
    61	
    62	    success: bool
    63	    entry_id: str | None = None
    64	    error: str | None = None
    65	
    66	    @classmethod
    67	    def from_dict(cls, data: dict[str, Any]) -> "AuditResult":
    68	        return cls(
    69	            success=data.get("success", False),
    70	            entry_id=data.get("entry_id") or data.get("id"),
    71	            error=data.get("error"),
    72	        )
    73	
    74	
    75	class AuditService:
    76	    """Service for audit trail logging and querying."""
    77	
    78	    def __init__(self, db: DatabaseClient | None = None):
    79	        self._db = db
    80	        #: Strong references to in-flight fire-and-forget insert tasks.
    81	        #:
    82	        #: ``asyncio`` keeps only a *weak* reference to a task, so a bare
    83	        #: ``create_task(...)`` whose result nobody holds may be garbage
    84	        #: collected before it runs. Holding the task until it completes is the
    85	        #: documented way to make fire-and-forget actually fire.
    86	        self._pending: set[asyncio.Task[AuditResult]] = set()
    87	
    88	    @property
    89	    def db(self) -> DatabaseClient:
    90	        if self._db is None:
    91	            self._db = get_db()
    92	        return self._db
    93	
    94	    async def log_operation(
    95	        self,
    96	        agent_id: str | None = None,
    97	        agent_type: str | None = None,
    98	        operation: str = "",
    99	        parameters: dict[str, Any] | None = None,
   100	        result: dict[str, Any] | None = None,
   101	        duration_ms: int | None = None,
   102	        success: bool | None = None,
   103	        error_message: str | None = None,
   104	        delegated_from: str | None = None,
   105	        session_id: str | None = None,
   106	    ) -> AuditResult:
   107	        """Log a coordination operation to the audit trail.
   108	
   109	        When async_logging is enabled (default), this fires-and-forgets
   110	        the insert to avoid blocking the caller.
   111	
   112	        Also pushes the entry into the audit-triage ring buffer (D9)
   113	        for downstream LLM classification.  The push is synchronous
   114	        and microsecond-fast — no LLM involvement on the hot path.
   115	        """
   116	        config = get_config()
   117	        agent_id = agent_id or config.agent.agent_id
   118	        agent_type = agent_type or config.agent.agent_type
   119	
   120	        data = {
   121	            "agent_id": agent_id,
   122	            "agent_type": agent_type,
   123	            "operation": operation,
   124	            "parameters": parameters or {},
   125	            "result": result or {},
   126	            "duration_ms": duration_ms,
   127	            "success": success,
   128	            "error_message": error_message,
   129	            "delegated_from": delegated_from,
   130	        }
   131	
   132	        # Push to audit-triage ring buffer (D9: hot path, no LLM)
   133	        try:
   134	            from .audit_triage import get_triage_buffer
   135	
   136	            entry = AuditEntry(
   137	                id="",
   138	                agent_id=agent_id,
   139	                agent_type=agent_type,
   140	                operation=operation,
   141	                parameters=parameters or {},
   142	                result=result or {},
   143	                duration_ms=duration_ms,
   144	                success=success,
   145	                error_message=error_message,
   146	                delegated_from=delegated_from,
   147	            )
   148	            resolved_session_id = session_id or (config.agent.session_id or "unknown")
   149	            get_triage_buffer().push(entry, session_id=resolved_session_id)
   150	        except Exception:
   151	            # Never let triage buffer failures affect the audit hot path
   152	            pass
   153	
   154	        if config.audit.async_logging:
   155	            # Fire-and-forget: don't block the caller. `success=True` here means
   156	            # "accepted for writing", not "written" — the insert has not run yet.
   157	            task = asyncio.create_task(self._insert_audit_entry(data))
   158	            self._pending.add(task)
   159	            task.add_done_callback(self._pending.discard)
   160	            return AuditResult(success=True)
   161	        else:
   162	            return await self._insert_audit_entry(data)
   163	
   164	    async def drain(self, timeout: float = 5.0) -> None:
   165	        """Wait for in-flight fire-and-forget audit inserts to finish.
   166	
   167	        Callers that need the trail to exist before they continue — startup
   168	        projections, shutdown, and tests — await this. Without it a short-lived
   169	        process can exit before the loop ever runs the queued inserts, which is
   170	        indistinguishable from the writes failing.
   171	
   172	        Raises:
   173	            TimeoutError: if ``timeout`` elapses while inserts are still
   174	                outstanding. ``asyncio.wait`` returns a ``(done, pending)``
   175	                pair rather than raising on timeout, so a caller that ignores
   176	                it would see ``drain()`` return normally and believe the
   177	                audit trail is durable when it is not — the same
   178	                returned-but-unread failure mode ``_insert_audit_entry``
   179	                documents, one layer up. Raising makes the timeout
   180	                impossible to silently ignore.
   181	        """
   182	        if not self._pending:
   183	            return
   184	        done, pending = await asyncio.wait(set(self._pending), timeout=timeout)
   185	        if pending:
   186	            logger.error(
   187	                "Audit drain timed out after %.1fs with %d insert(s) still "
   188	                "outstanding — the audit trail is not guaranteed durable.",
   189	                timeout,
   190	                len(pending),
   191	            )
   192	            raise TimeoutError(
   193	                f"AuditService.drain() timed out after {timeout}s with "
   194	                f"{len(pending)} audit insert(s) still outstanding"
   195	            )
   196	
   197	    async def _insert_audit_entry(self, data: dict[str, Any]) -> AuditResult:
   198	        """Insert an audit entry into the database.
   199	
   200	        Failures are logged rather than only returned. On the fire-and-forget
   201	        path nobody awaits the result, so a returned-but-unread error is the
   202	        same as no error at all — which is exactly how the audit trail came to
   203	        record nothing at all on the PostgreSQL backend for every operation:
   204	        ``log_operation`` built a payload containing ``delegated_from``, a
   205	        column ``audit_log`` did not have until migration 035, so every insert
   206	        raised, the exception was swallowed here, the failed result was
   207	        discarded by the caller, and callers were told ``success=True``.
   208	        """
   209	        try:
   210	            row = await self.db.insert("audit_log", data)
   211	            return AuditResult(success=True, entry_id=str(row.get("id", "")))
   212	        except Exception as e:
   213	            logger.error(
   214	                "Audit write failed for operation %r — the audit trail is "
   215	                "incomplete: %s",
   216	                data.get("operation"),
   217	                e,
   218	                exc_info=True,
   219	            )
   220	            return AuditResult(success=False, error=str(e))
   221	
   222	    async def query(
   223	        self,
   224	        agent_id: str | None = None,
   225	        operation: str | None = None,
   226	        since: datetime | None = None,
   227	        until: datetime | None = None,
   228	        limit: int = 50,
   229	        delegated_from: str | None = None,
   230	        change_id: str | None = None,
   231	    ) -> list[AuditEntry]:
   232	        """Query audit log entries with optional filters.
   233	
   234	        New filters (additive, backward-compatible; all optional):
   235	        - ``since``: ISO-8601 timestamp; returns entries with
   236	          ``created_at >= since``.
   237	        - ``change_id``: filters entries whose ``parameters`` JSONB column
   238	          contains ``{"change_id": "<id>"}`` (recorded by most call-sites)
   239	          OR whose ``agent_id`` maps to an ``agent_sessions.change_id``
   240	          match (fallback, best-effort).
   241	        """
   242	        query_parts = ["order=created_at.desc", f"limit={limit}"]
   243	
   244	        if agent_id:
   245	            query_parts.append(f"agent_id=eq.{agent_id}")
   246	        if operation:
   247	            query_parts.append(f"operation=eq.{operation}")
   248	        if since:
   249	            query_parts.append(f"created_at=gte.{since.isoformat()}")
   250	        if until:
   251	            query_parts.append(f"created_at=lte.{until.isoformat()}")
   252	        if delegated_from:
   253	            query_parts.append(f"delegated_from=eq.{delegated_from}")
   254	        if change_id:
   255	            # Filter on parameters JSONB containing change_id key.
   256	            # PostgREST/Supabase: parameters->>change_id=eq.<value>
   257	            # PostgresClient: appended as a raw query param string.
   258	            query_parts.append(f"parameters->>change_id=eq.{change_id}")
   259	
   260	        query = "&".join(query_parts)
   261	        rows = await self.db.query("audit_log", query)
   262	        return [AuditEntry.from_dict(row) for row in rows]
   263	
   264	    def timed(self, operation: str) -> "AuditTimer":
   265	        """Create a context manager for timing and logging an operation."""
   266	        return AuditTimer(self, operation)
   267	
   268	
   269	class AuditTimer:
   270	    """Context manager for timing operations and logging to audit trail."""
   271	
   272	    def __init__(self, service: AuditService, operation: str):
   273	        self.service = service
   274	        self.operation = operation
   275	        self._start: float = 0
   276	
   277	    async def __aenter__(self) -> "AuditTimer":
   278	        self._start = time.monotonic()
   279	        return self
   280	
   281	    async def __aexit__(
   282	        self,
   283	        exc_type: type[BaseException] | None,
   284	        exc_val: BaseException | None,
   285	        exc_tb: Any,
   286	    ) -> None:
   287	        duration_ms = int((time.monotonic() - self._start) * 1000)
   288	        await self.service.log_operation(
   289	            operation=self.operation,
   290	            duration_ms=duration_ms,
   291	            success=exc_type is None,
   292	            error_message=str(exc_val) if exc_val else None,
   293	        )
   294	
   295	
   296	# Global service instance
   297	_audit_service: AuditService | None = None
   298	
   299	
   300	def get_audit_service() -> AuditService:
   301	    """Get the global audit service instance."""
   302	    global _audit_service
   303	    if _audit_service is None:
   304	        _audit_service = AuditService()
   305	    return _audit_service

   120	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   121	# Archetype name pattern (shared between schema and runtime validation)
   122	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   123	
   124	# The supervisor archetype is a read-only orchestrator: it decomposes work,
   125	# delegates it to write-capable worker archetypes, and adjudicates gates. It
   126	# MUST NOT be write-capable — every code change is dispatched, never made by
   127	# the supervisor itself. The archetype resolver enforces this invariant at
   128	# config-load time (fail-loud), mirroring the D3 structured-field enforcement
   129	# that a write-capable phase must resolve to a write_capable archetype.
   130	SUPERVISOR_ARCHETYPE: str = "supervisor"
   131	
   132	ARCHETYPE_NAME_PATTERN = r"^[a-z][a-z0-9_-]{0,31}$"
   133	
   134	# A tier entry: bare model-id string, or model paired with a thinking level.
   135	# Thinking vocabularies are vendor-specific (Claude effort tiers, Codex
   136	# model_reasoning_effort, grok thinking budgets), so the value is a free
   137	# string — the dispatching adapter owns translation to CLI flags.
   138	_TIER_VALUE_SCHEMA: dict[str, Any] = {
   139	    "oneOf": [
   140	        {"type": "string", "minLength": 1},

   142	            "type": "object",

   144	            "additionalProperties": False,

   149	        },

   227	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   228	# Procedure mode (OpenSpec change add-skill-audit, design D3)
   229	#
   230	# How much of a skill's written procedure an agent running under an archetype
   231	# is expected to follow. It is a property of the archetype (the role), not of
   232	# the tier it escalates to. `guided` is the default and appends nothing, so a
   233	# roster that never declares the field resolves byte-identically to before.
   234	# The sentences are defined once, here, and injected at exactly one place:
   235	# resolve_archetype_for_phase. Tests import these constants rather than
   236	# restating the text.
   237	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   238	
   239	PROCEDURE_MODES: tuple[str, ...] = ("verbatim", "guided", "goal-directed")
   240	DEFAULT_PROCEDURE_MODE = "guided"
   241	PROCEDURE_MODE_SENTENCES: dict[str, str] = {
   242	    "verbatim": (
   243	        "Follow the skill's written procedure step by step; do not skip, "
   244	        "reorder, or merge steps."

   246	    "goal-directed": (
   247	        "Satisfy the skill's acceptance probes by whatever route is sound; "

   555	class PollConfig:
   556	    """Polling configuration for versioned JSON vendor envelopes."""

   558	    command_template: list[str]
   559	    result_protocol: str = "vendor-envelope-v1"

   561	    timeout_seconds: int = 600

   565	class ModeConfig:
   566	    """CLI args for a single dispatch mode."""
   567	
   568	    args: list[str]
   569	    async_dispatch: bool = False
   570	    poll: PollConfig | None = None
   571	    isolation: IsolationMode | None = None
   572	
   573	
   574	@dataclass
   575	class CliConfig:
   576	    """CLI dispatch configuration for an agent.
   577	
   578	    Parsed from the ``cli`` section of an agent entry in ``agents.yaml``.
   579	    """
   580	
   581	    command: str
   582	    dispatch_modes: dict[str, ModeConfig]
   583	    model_flag: str
   584	    model: str | None = None
   585	    model_fallbacks: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)
   586	    prompt_via_stdin: bool = False
   587	    # When set, the dispatching adapter attaches the prompt as this flag's
   588	    # value (``[prompt_via_flag, prompt]``) instead of via stdin or a trailing
   589	    # positional. Antigravity needs this: its prompt is the value of
   590	    # ``--prompt``/``--print`` and stdin is ignored (design.md E7).
   591	    prompt_via_flag: str = ""
   592	    # Env var the CLI resolves its provider credential from (pi:
   593	    # OPENROUTER_API_KEY). A present binary with this var unset cannot serve
   594	    # a request, so availability checks fail closed on it (issue #383).
   595	    api_key_env: str = ""
   596

   722	class ProviderModelMappingError(ValueError):
   723	    """Raised when a logical/legacy model cannot resolve for a provider."""
   724	
   725	    def __init__(self, provider: str, model: str, tier: str | None = None) -> None:
   726	        self.provider = provider
   727	        self.model = model
   728	        self.tier = tier
   729	        if tier:
   730	            message = (
   731	                f"missing provider model mapping for provider={provider!r}, "
   732	                f"tier={tier!r}, source_model={model!r}"
   733	            )
   734	        else:
   735	            message = (
   736	                f"missing provider model mapping for provider={provider!r}, "
   737	                f"source_model={model!r}"
   738	            )
   739	        super().__init__(message)
   740	
   741	
   742	class LocalRosterConfigError(ValueError):
   743	    """Raised at startup when a `local` roster entry breaks a hardware rule.
   744	
   745	    Structured on purpose (``rule`` / ``tier`` / ``detail``): an unattended
   746	    loop must be able to say which rule was violated, not just that the config
   747	    is bad. Uses the same fail-fast mechanism as the undefined-archetype
   748	    ``ValueError`` in :func:`load_archetypes_config`.
   749	    """
   750	
   751	    def __init__(self, rule: str, detail: str, *, tier: str | None = None) -> None:
   752	        self.rule = rule
   753	        self.tier = tier
   754	        self.detail = detail
   755	        location = (
   756	            f"model_aliases.{LOCAL_PROVIDER}.{tier}"
   757	            if tier
   758	            else f"model_aliases.{LOCAL_PROVIDER}"
   759	        )
   760	        super().__init__(f"invalid local roster at {location}: {rule} — {detail}")

     1	"""Provider-neutral autopilot phase dispatch adapters.
     2	
     3	Scope note for the built-in `local` adapter: its concurrency cap
     4	(``LOCAL_INFERENCE_MAX_CONCURRENCY``) is enforced **per process**, not host-wide.
     5	The gate is a :class:`threading.Semaphore` owned by this module, so N concurrent
     6	autopilot processes pointed at the same endpoint can each admit up to the cap —

    97	# --- local provider adapter (OpenSpec add-local-model-provider-tier, D2/D5) ---
    98	#
    99	# `local` launches the existing Pi coding-agent harness with its normal file and
   100	# command tools. A one-shot Pi extension registers the distinct `local` provider
   101	# against the operator-run OpenAI-compatible endpoint (llama-server / vLLM /
   102	# Ollama); stdlib urllib remains only for the bounded health probe.
   103	#
   104	# Environment contract:
   105	#   LOCAL_INFERENCE_BASE_URL       required to enable; http:// or https:// only;
   106	#                                  includes the API version prefix, e.g.
   107	#                                  "http://gx10.local:8080/v1"
   108	#   LOCAL_INFERENCE_API_KEY        optional bearer token
   109	#   LOCAL_INFERENCE_MAX_CONCURRENCY  optional, default 4, clamped to 64; excess
   110	#                                  dispatches queue (per process — see the module
   111	#                                  docstring)
   112	#
   113	# With LOCAL_INFERENCE_BASE_URL unset the provider is inert: dispatch returns the
   114	# same structured `fallback` result any unconfigured adapter returns, and no
   115	# network call is made (Rule 4 — safe default).
   116	_LOCAL_PROVIDER = "local"
   117	_LOCAL_DEFAULT_MAX_CONCURRENCY = 4
   118	# A process cannot usefully hold more in-flight local requests than this, and a
   119	# fat-fingered env value must not turn the gate into an unbounded thread farm.
   120	_LOCAL_MAX_MAX_CONCURRENCY = 64
   121	# Only these schemes are dispatchable; anything else (file:, ftp:, a bare host)
   122	# is a misconfiguration, not an endpoint.
   123	_LOCAL_ALLOWED_SCHEMES = ("http", "https")
   124	# Short by design: a dead endpoint must surface as adapter unavailability in
   125	# seconds, never as a stalled phase.
   126	_LOCAL_PROBE_TIMEOUT_SECONDS = 3.0
   127	# Bounded wall-clock ceiling for the headless Pi agent process.
   128	_LOCAL_DISPATCH_TIMEOUT_SECONDS = 300
   129	# Upper bound on time spent queued behind the concurrency cap. Queueing is
   130	# required by the spec (excess dispatches queue, they are never dropped), but it
   131	# must still terminate: a wedged slot holder degrades the waiter to the
   132	# structured fallback instead of parking the phase forever.
   133	_LOCAL_GATE_ACQUIRE_TIMEOUT_SECONDS = 1800
   134	# The probe verdict is a cache, not a fact. A short TTL keeps a restarted or
   135	# just-crashed endpoint from being pinned to a stale verdict for the whole
   136	# process lifetime, in either direction.
   137	_LOCAL_PROBE_TTL_SECONDS = 30.0
   138	# Responses are JSON handoffs, not model weights: anything past this budget is a
   139	# misbehaving endpoint and fails closed to the structured fallback.
   140	_LOCAL_MAX_RESPONSE_BYTES = 10 * 1024 * 1024
   141	_LOCAL_PI_EXTENSION = Path(__file__).with_name("pi_local_provider.ts")
   142	# Defence in depth for the resolver-side trust boundary (design D3). The
   143	# coordinator is the single decision point, but a payload can reach this adapter
   144	# from any client; an archetype outside this allowlist never reaches the wire.
   145	_LOCAL_TRUSTED_ARCHETYPES = frozenset({"runner", "analyst", "documenter", "validator"})
   146

   148	class LocalAdapterError(RuntimeError):
   149	    """Base for adapter-side local failures. Never escapes ``dispatch_phase``."""
   150	
   151	
   152	class LocalDeadlineExceeded(LocalAdapterError, TimeoutError):
   153	    """The HTTP health probe exceeded its wall-clock deadline."""
   154	
   155	
   156	class LocalGateTimeout(LocalAdapterError, TimeoutError):
   157	    """Waiting for a concurrency slot blew its bound."""
   158	
   159	
   160	class LocalResponseTooLarge(LocalAdapterError, ValueError):
   161	    """The endpoint sent more bytes than the response budget allows."""
   162	
   163	
   164	_local_state_lock = threading.Lock()
   165	# Serializes cold probes so concurrent first-callers issue one request, not N.
   166	_local_probe_lock = threading.Lock()
   167	# (base_url, reachable, expires_at_monotonic) — TTL'd, and invalidated whenever a
   168	# dispatch hits a connection error.
   169	_local_probe_cache: tuple[str, bool, float] | None = None
   170	_local_gate_semaphore: threading.Semaphore | None = None
   171	_local_gate_limit: int | None = None
   172	
   173	
   174	def reset_local_adapter_state() -> None:
   175	    """Drop the cached health probe and concurrency gate (test hook)."""
   176	    global _local_probe_cache, _local_gate_semaphore, _local_gate_limit
   177	    with _local_state_lock:
   178	        _local_probe_cache = None
   179	        _local_gate_semaphore = None
   180	        _local_gate_limit = None
   181	
   182	
   183	def invalidate_local_probe_cache() -> None:
   184	    """Forget the cached probe verdict; the next caller re-probes."""
   185	    global _local_probe_cache
   186	    with _local_state_lock:
   187	        _local_probe_cache = None

   190	class _ReadableResponse(Protocol):
   191	    def read(self, amount: int = -1) -> bytes: ...
   192	
   193	
   194	def _read_capped(resp: _ReadableResponse) -> bytes:
   195	    """Read at most :data:`_LOCAL_MAX_RESPONSE_BYTES` from *resp*, else fail."""
   196	    chunk = resp.read(_LOCAL_MAX_RESPONSE_BYTES + 1)
   197	    if len(chunk) > _LOCAL_MAX_RESPONSE_BYTES:
   198	        raise LocalResponseTooLarge(
   199	            f"response exceeded the {_LOCAL_MAX_RESPONSE_BYTES}-byte budget"
   200	        )
   201	    return chunk

   203	
   204	def _http_get_json(url: str, headers: dict[str, str], timeout: float) -> dict[str, Any]:
   205	    """Real HTTP GET transport used only by the bounded health probe."""
   206	    req = urllib.request.Request(url, headers=headers, method="GET")
   207	    with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=timeout) as resp:  # noqa: S310
   208	        parsed: Any = json.loads(_read_capped(resp).decode("utf-8"))
   209	    if not isinstance(parsed, dict):
   210	        raise LocalAdapterError("local health probe returned a non-object body")
   211	    return parsed

   213	
   214	def _call_with_deadline(fn: Callable[[], Any], deadline_seconds: float) -> Any:
   215	    """Run *fn* under a wall-clock deadline.
   216	
   217	    ``urllib``'s ``timeout`` is per socket operation: an endpoint that trickles a
   218	    byte every few seconds never trips it. A bounded worker gives probe and
   219	    dispatch a real ceiling — the caller is released at the deadline (freeing its
   220	    concurrency slot) while the abandoned request is left to the daemon thread.
   221	    """
   222	    box: dict[str, Any] = {}
   223	
   224	    def _run() -> None:
   225	        try:
   226	            box["value"] = fn()
   227	        except BaseException as exc:  # noqa: BLE001 — re-raised in the caller
   228	            box["error"] = exc
   229	
   230	    worker = threading.Thread(target=_run, daemon=True)
   231	    worker.start()
   232	    worker.join(deadline_seconds)
   233	    if worker.is_alive():
   234	        raise LocalDeadlineExceeded(
   235	            f"local endpoint did not answer within {deadline_seconds}s"
   236	        )
   237	    if "error" in box:
   238	        raise box["error"]
   239	    return box.get("value")
   240	
   241	
   242	def _is_connection_error(exc: BaseException) -> bool:
   243	    """Whether *exc* casts doubt on endpoint reachability (probe invalidation)."""
   244	    return isinstance(exc, (OSError, LocalDeadlineExceeded, LocalGateTimeout))
   245

   247	def _local_base_url_raw() -> str:
   248	    return os.environ.get("LOCAL_INFERENCE_BASE_URL", "").strip().rstrip("/")
   249	
   250	
   251	def _local_base_url() -> str | None:
   252	    """The configured endpoint, or None when unset or not an http(s) URL."""
   253	    raw = _local_base_url_raw()
   254	    if not raw:
   255	        return None
   256	    if urllib.parse.urlsplit(raw).scheme.lower() not in _LOCAL_ALLOWED_SCHEMES:
   257	        return None
   258	    return raw
   259	
   260	
   261	def _local_headers() -> dict[str, str]:
   262	    headers = {"Content-Type": "application/json"}
   263	    api_key = os.environ.get("LOCAL_INFERENCE_API_KEY", "").strip()
   264	    if api_key:
   265	        headers["Authorization"] = f"Bearer {api_key}"
   266	    return headers
   267	
   268	
   269	def _local_max_concurrency() -> int:
   270	    """Simultaneous local dispatches; anything unparseable or <=0 uses the default."""
   271	    try:
   272	        value = int(os.environ.get("LOCAL_INFERENCE_MAX_CONCURRENCY", "").strip())
   273	    except ValueError:
   274	        return _LOCAL_DEFAULT_MAX_CONCURRENCY
   275	    if value <= 0:
   276	        return _LOCAL_DEFAULT_MAX_CONCURRENCY
   277	    if value > _LOCAL_MAX_MAX_CONCURRENCY:
   278	        logger.warning(
   279	            "LOCAL_INFERENCE_MAX_CONCURRENCY=%s clamped to %s",
   280	            value,
   281	            _LOCAL_MAX_MAX_CONCURRENCY,
   282	        )
   283	        return _LOCAL_MAX_MAX_CONCURRENCY
   284	    return value
   285	
   286	
   287	def _local_gate() -> threading.Semaphore:
   288	    """Concurrency cap. Excess dispatches block (queue), they are never dropped.
   289	
   290	    The cap is read from the environment exactly once (first use, or after
   291	    :func:`reset_local_adapter_state`). Re-reading it per dispatch would let a
   292	    mid-run env change swap the semaphore out from under in-flight holders, and
   293	    the new gate would admit its full limit on top of them.
   294	    """
   295	    global _local_gate_semaphore, _local_gate_limit
   296	    with _local_state_lock:
   297	        if _local_gate_semaphore is None:
   298	            _local_gate_limit = _local_max_concurrency()
   299	            _local_gate_semaphore = threading.Semaphore(_local_gate_limit)
   300	        return _local_gate_semaphore
   301	
   302	
   303	def _cached_probe_verdict(base_url: str) -> bool | None:
   304	    """The unexpired cached verdict for *base_url*, or None when it must re-probe."""
   305	    with _local_state_lock:
   306	        cached = _local_probe_cache
   307	    if cached is None or cached[0] != base_url:
   308	        return None
   309	    if time.monotonic() >= cached[2]:
   310	        return None
   311	    return cached[1]
   312	
   313	
   314	def local_endpoint_available(*, force: bool = False) -> bool:
   315	    """Whether the configured local endpoint answered its health probe.
   316	
   317	    Probes ``GET {LOCAL_INFERENCE_BASE_URL}/models`` (the OpenAI-compatible model
   318	    listing) with a short timeout and caches the verdict for
   319	    :data:`_LOCAL_PROBE_TTL_SECONDS`. The TTL matters in both directions: a
   320	    single transient failure must not blackhole `local` for the rest of the
   321	    process, and an endpoint that dies after one good probe must not stay
   322	    "available" forever. A dispatch-time connection error additionally
   323	    invalidates the cache immediately.
   324	
   325	    Returns False when no endpoint is configured, or when the configured value is
   326	    not an http(s) URL — callers (dispatch, and the roadmap policy engine's
   327	    switch-target selection) treat that as "adapter unavailable", never an error.
   328	    """
   329	    global _local_probe_cache
   330	    base_url = _local_base_url()
   331	    if base_url is None:
   332	        raw = _local_base_url_raw()
   333	        if raw:
   334	            logger.warning(
   335	                "local adapter unavailable: LOCAL_INFERENCE_BASE_URL must use one "
   336	                "of %s (got scheme %r)",
   337	                "/".join(_LOCAL_ALLOWED_SCHEMES),
   338	                urllib.parse.urlsplit(raw).scheme,
   339	            )
   340	        return False
   341	
   342	    if not force:
   343	        cached = _cached_probe_verdict(base_url)
   344	        if cached is not None:
   345	            return cached
   346	
   347	    # Single-flight: concurrent cold callers collapse onto one probe.
   348	    with _local_probe_lock:
   349	        if not force:
   350	            cached = _cached_probe_verdict(base_url)
   351	            if cached is not None:
   352	                return cached
   353	        try:
   354	            _call_with_deadline(
   355	                lambda: _http_get_json(
   356	                    f"{base_url}/models",
   357	                    _local_headers(),
   358	                    _LOCAL_PROBE_TIMEOUT_SECONDS,
   359	                ),
   360	                _LOCAL_PROBE_TIMEOUT_SECONDS,
   361	            )
   362	            reachable = True
   363	        except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001 — any probe failure is unavailability
   364	            logger.debug("local health probe failed for %s: %s", base_url, exc)
   365	            reachable = False
   366	
   367	        with _local_state_lock:
   368	            _local_probe_cache = (
   369	                base_url,
   370	                reachable,
   371	                time.monotonic() + _LOCAL_PROBE_TTL_SECONDS,
   372	            )
   373	        return reachable
   374	
   375	
   376	def normalize_dispatch_result(
   377	    raw: Any,
   378	    payload: PhaseDispatchPayload,
   379	    dispatch_tier: str,
   380	) -> PhaseDispatchResult:
   381	    """Normalize tuple/dict adapter output into the contract result shape."""
   382	    warnings: list[str] = []
   383	    outcome: str | None = None
   384	    handoff_id: str | None = None
   385	    model_used = payload.model
   386	    error_class: str | None = None
   387	    capacity_scope: str | None = None
   388	    capacity_model: str | None = None
   389	    capacity_reset_at: str | None = None
   390	    capacity_retry_after_seconds: int | None = None
   391	
   392	    if isinstance(raw, tuple) and len(raw) == 2:
   393	        outcome, handoff_id = raw
   394	    elif isinstance(raw, dict):
   395	        outcome = raw.get("outcome")
   396	        handoff_id = raw.get("handoff_id")
   397	        model_used = raw.get("model_used", model_used)
   398	        error_class = raw.get("error_class")
   399	        capacity_scope = raw.get("capacity_scope")
   400	        capacity_model = raw.get("capacity_model")
   401	        capacity_reset_at = raw.get("capacity_reset_at")
   402	        capacity_retry_after_seconds = raw.get("capacity_retry_after_seconds")
   403	        raw_warnings = raw.get("warnings")
   404	        if isinstance(raw_warnings, list):
   405	            warnings = [str(item) for item in raw_warnings]
   406	
   407	    if not isinstance(outcome, str) or not outcome:
   408	        outcome = "failed"
   409	        warnings.append("adapter returned missing outcome")
   410	    if not isinstance(handoff_id, str) or not handoff_id:
   411	        digest = hashlib.sha256(
   412	            json.dumps(payload.to_dict(), sort_keys=True).encode("utf-8")
   413	        ).hexdigest()[:12]
   414	        handoff_id = f"{dispatch_tier}:{payload.provider}:{payload.phase}:{digest}"
   415	        warnings.append("adapter returned missing handoff_id")
   416	
   417	    return PhaseDispatchResult(
   418	        outcome=outcome,
   419	        handoff_id=handoff_id,
   420	        provider=payload.provider,
   421	        model_used=model_used,
   422	        dispatch_tier=dispatch_tier,
   423	        warnings=warnings,
   424	        agent_id=payload.agent_id,
   425	        error_class=error_class,
   426	        capacity_scope=capacity_scope,
   427	        capacity_model=capacity_model,
   428	        capacity_reset_at=capacity_reset_at,
   429	        capacity_retry_after_seconds=capacity_retry_after_seconds,
   430	    )
   431	
   432	
   433	def _fallback_result(
   434	    payload: PhaseDispatchPayload,
   435	    warning: str,
   436	) -> PhaseDispatchResult:
   437	    """The structured degradation every unconfigured adapter returns."""
   438	    return PhaseDispatchResult(
   439	        outcome="failed",
   440	        handoff_id=f"fallback:{payload.provider}:{payload.phase}",
   441	        provider=payload.provider,
   442	        model_used=payload.model,
   443	        dispatch_tier="fallback",
   444	        warnings=[warning],
   445	        agent_id=payload.agent_id,
   446	    )

   448	
   449	def _local_harness_prompt(payload: PhaseDispatchPayload) -> str:
   450	    """Build the phase prompt consumed by the tool-capable Pi agent harness."""
   451	    expected = ", ".join(payload.expected_outcomes) or "complete, failed"
   452	    result_contract = json.dumps(
   453	        {
   454	            "outcome": f"<one of: {expected}>",
   455	            "handoff_id": "<real handoff id>",
   456	        },
   457	        separators=(",", ":"),
   458	    )
   459	    sections = [
   460	        payload.system_prompt or "You are a focused phase agent.",
   461	        payload.prompt,
   462	        (
   463	            "Use the coding-agent tools to inspect files, run commands, and make "
   464	            "only the changes required by this phase. A text-only answer is not a "
   465	            "completed phase. Before finishing, write a durable handoff through the "
   466	            "configured coordinator handoff capability (or its documented local "
   467	            "fallback). Your final assistant message must be only this JSON shape: "
   468	            f"{result_contract}. Never invent or omit the handoff id."
   469	        ),
   470	    ]
   471	    return (chr(10) * 2).join(sections)

   474	def _run_local_agent_cli(
   475	    payload: PhaseDispatchPayload,
   476	) -> subprocess.CompletedProcess[str]:
   477	    """Run Pi headlessly with the local endpoint registered as a provider."""
   478	    if not _LOCAL_PI_EXTENSION.is_file():
   479	        raise LocalAdapterError("local Pi provider extension is missing")
   480	    env = os.environ.copy()
   481	    env["LOCAL_INFERENCE_MODEL"] = payload.model or ""
   482	    command = [
   483	        "pi",
   484	        "-p",
   485	        "--provider",
   486	        "local",
   487	        "--model",
   488	        payload.model or "",
   489	        "--mode",
   490	        "json",
   491	        "--approve",
   492	        "--no-session",
   493	        "--extension",
   494	        str(_LOCAL_PI_EXTENSION),
   495	        _local_harness_prompt(payload),
   496	    ]
   497	    return subprocess.run(  # noqa: S603 -- fixed executable and list-form args
   498	        command,
   499	        capture_output=True,
   500	        text=True,
   501	        timeout=_LOCAL_DISPATCH_TIMEOUT_SECONDS,
   502	        env=env,
   503	        check=False,
   504	    )

   507	def _assistant_text(message: Any) -> str | None:
   508	    """Extract assistant text from a Pi JSON-mode message payload."""
   509	    if not isinstance(message, dict) or message.get("role") != "assistant":
   510	        return None
   511	    content = message.get("content")
   512	    if isinstance(content, str):
   513	        return content
   514	    if isinstance(content, list):
   515	        parts = [
   516	            part["text"]
   517	            for part in content
   518	            if isinstance(part, dict) and isinstance(part.get("text"), str)
   519	        ]
   520	        return chr(10).join(parts) if parts else None
   521	    return None
   522	
   523	
   524	def _parse_local_harness_output(stdout: str) -> dict[str, Any] | None:
   525	    """Return the last explicit outcome and handoff id from Pi NDJSON."""
   526	    last_text: str | None = None
   527	    for line in stdout.splitlines():
   528	        try:
   529	            event = json.loads(line)
   530	        except json.JSONDecodeError:
   531	            continue
   532	        if not isinstance(event, dict):
   533	            continue
   534	        text = _assistant_text(event.get("message"))
   535	        if text:
   536	            last_text = text
   537	    if last_text is None:
   538	        return None
   539	    try:
   540	        parsed = json.loads(last_text)
   541	    except json.JSONDecodeError:
   542	        return None
   543	    if not isinstance(parsed, dict):
   544	        return None
   545	    outcome = parsed.get("outcome")
   546	    handoff_id = parsed.get("handoff_id")
   547	    if (
   548	        not isinstance(outcome, str)
   549	        or not outcome.strip()
   550	        or not isinstance(handoff_id, str)
   551	        or not handoff_id.strip()
   552	    ):
   553	        return None
   554	    return parsed
