1	The plan never names the seam that carries the dg-06 routing decision into the two execution sinks, so the scenario 'Routed execution is not re-resolved' (specs/vendor-dispatch/spec.md:28-32) cannot be satisfied as tasked. PhaseDispatchPayload (provider_dispatch.py:39-66) has no decision_id, worktree_root, dispatch_mode, location, or source, yet DispatchExecutionContext requires worktree_root and source and is keyed by decision_id (contracts/dispatch-execution-context.schema.json:7-24). CliVendorAdapter.dispatch()/dispatch_async() (review_dispatcher.py:944-948, 1431-1435) accept no execution context at all. dg-06 attaches routing only to the roadmap host context (autopilot-roadmap/scripts/orchestrator.py:1653-1661), which the SKILL.md layer consumes, not these Python sinks. Tasks 4.2/4.3 say 'using its immutable payload' without a payload schema bump or an adapter kwarg. Specify: (a) PhaseDispatchPayload schema_version 2 carrying an embedded DispatchExecutionContext, (b) an explicit `execution_context` parameter on dispatch/dispatch_async/poll_for_result and the review CLI entry points, and (c) the rule for isolation=none passthrough when worktree_root is absent (today _run_local_agent_cli inherits cwd, provider_dispatch.py:497-504).	fix
2	Review mode renders `filesystem.allowWrite: []` and the only behavioral evidence (tasks.md:38-39) uses a controlled fixture, so real vendor CLIs are never exercised under the sandbox before rollout. SRT 0.0.77 leaves only /tmp/claude, ~/.npm/_logs and ~/.claude/debug writable by default; `claude -p` writes ~/.claude/projects and ~/.claude.json, `codex exec` writes ~/.codex/sessions and ~/.codex/log, `pi` writes ~/.pi. Under the planned review policy every real vendor lane will fail or degrade for a reason the plan does not anticipate, and the roadmap acceptance outcome (openspec/roadmaps/dispatch-governance/roadmap.yaml, dg-07 'observable restriction on a dispatched vendor CLI') requires a real CLI. Add a per-vendor writable-state inventory (authored in agents.yaml, not hard-coded in the renderer, consistent with D4), extend 5.1/5.2 with at least one real vendor CLI run, and state whether those state directories are writable in review mode or whether vendors must be launched with an isolated HOME/XDG state root under the runtime temp directory.	fix
3	D3 confines write-capable modes to the canonical worktree root and denies common Git metadata, but the per-worktree gitdir (<common>/.git/worktrees/<name>/ holding index, HEAD, ORIG_HEAD, logs) also lives outside the root. With bubblewrap read-only mounts, `git add`, `git commit`, `git stash`, and index refresh fail inside the sandbox. The repo's own conventions require implementers to make save-point commits (AGENTS.md git conventions; implement-feature/autopilot prompts), and the review snapshot fallback in review_dispatcher.py:2416-2458 assumes vendors can at least read a linked worktree whose `.git` file points outside the root. The plan says 'the host owns commit/merge' without changing any skill prompt or defining a host-side commit step. Decide explicitly: either grant the per-worktree gitdir plus objects/refs (accepting the shared-object risk D3 names) or add tasks to update implement-feature/autopilot/iterate prompts and the roadmap dispatch loop so sandboxed write-mode agents never attempt commits and the host commits after collection. Also note that `.git` inside a linked worktree root is a plain file the child can rewrite; add it to denyWrite.	escalate
4	The export grammar admits only a leading `*.` wildcard, but the authored table accepts `*` anywhere and matches via LIKE (agent-coordinator/database/migrations/009_network_policies.sql:12, 85-88), e.g. `*github.com` also matches `evilgithub.com`. The plan says a malformed snapshot renders deny-all (design.md:53-54) but does not say whether 'malformed' is per-rule or per-document. Dropping an unrenderable deny rule widens policy; failing the whole document on one unrenderable allow blocks every lane. Specify per-rule handling: unrenderable deny => deny-all (fail closed); unrenderable allow => omitted with a warning recorded in the export; and add a coordinator-side validation on write so new rules cannot enter the non-exportable grammar. Also define `policy_revision` concretely: network_policies has no updated_at or version column (009:9-18), so a revision string cannot detect enabled/priority edits; state that the digest is the only change detector or add a migration.	fix
5	Two environment questions are unresolved. (a) Which environment runs the fail-open 'original command'? D5 strips inherited HTTP(S)_PROXY/ALL_PROXY and loader variables; in a managed cloud harness the platform proxy is mandatory for egress, and SRT will always fail preflight there (no user namespaces, nested sandbox not configurable per D2). If the fallback reuses the sanitized env it breaks egress; the compatibility scenario (spec.md:16-20) requires byte-identical behavior. State that sanitization applies only when SRT is applied. (b) PATH policy: the pinned `srt` bin is a `#!/usr/bin/env node` shim (package.json bin -> dist/cli.js), vendor CLIs are node shims, and SRT locates bwrap/socat/rg via PATH. 'Absolute executable paths' plus a sanitized env is underspecified: either preserve a validated PATH or have preflight record absolute node/bwrap/socat/rg paths and launch `node /abs/dist/cli.js`. Note this host resolves node only from ~/.local/share/pi-node.	fix
6	Durable audit lacks idempotency. The outbox drain retries older entries on later calls, and a crash between a coordinator acknowledgement and the outbox entry removal replays the same event. audit_log has no uniqueness on an event id, and AuditService.log_operation with async_logging (agent-coordinator/src/audit.py:154-160) returns success before insertion, so task 2.4 must bypass it and define its own durability. Specify: the endpoint treats `event_id` (contracts/sandbox-execution-event.schema.json:20) as an idempotency key (unique index, 200 on replay), the outbox removes an entry only after acknowledgement, and the acknowledgement contract names the persisted row id. Also name the outbox location and its ownership: it must sit outside any worktree root a write-capable sandboxed child can reach and outside the repo checkout so it is never committed.	fix
7	The autopilot `local` provider is one of the two sinks the plan wraps, but its endpoint is env-authored (LOCAL_INFERENCE_BASE_URL, often a `.local` mDNS host, a private IP, or loopback, provider_dispatch.py:247-258) and never exists in coordinator policy. SRT's proxies additionally resolve hostnames and drop loopback/link-local/metadata addresses before dialing. Under isolation=sandbox the Pi harness can therefore never reach its model endpoint, and D4 (design.md:57-60) only discusses public vendor API domains. State either that `local` + sandbox fails closed with a named degradation reason until an authored private-endpoint rule (hostname:port, optional deniedResolvedAddresses exemption) exists, or add the authored-endpoint path for private hosts to the rollout inventory in 5.3.	fix
8	Async poll and cancel are required to go through the backend (spec.md:5-14), so a cold-start deny-all policy or coordinator outage makes every poll command fail. poll_for_result treats a nonzero poll exit as terminal and closes the completion ledger as failed (review_dispatcher.py:1703-1719), abandoning a vendor task that is still running remotely and cannot be collected. Either classify poll/cancel as control-plane (like discovery and health probes, spec.md:7-8) with a stated justification, or require the backend to distinguish 'sandbox denied egress' from a vendor status failure and have the poller retry until its deadline instead of finalizing the ledger.	fix
9	Work-package scope and verification do not cover tasks 5.1 and 5.2. wp-validation-docs may write only docs/** and openspec (166-171) but task 5.1 requires a controlled vendor fixture under skills/; its only verification step is `openspec validate --strict` (177-186), so no behavioral evidence is checked. wp-runtime's write_allow includes test_sandbox_profile_integration.py but its verification runs only test_sandbox_profile.py (96-105). The design requires 'at least one recorded capable-host pass' (design.md:121-123) yet CI is ubuntu-latest only (.github/workflows/ci.yml, all runs-on entries) with no macOS runner, and Ubuntu 24.04 restricts unprivileged user namespaces. Name the runner (or a self-hosted/manual job), the evidence artifact path the roadmap gate reads, and move the fixture into wp-runtime or widen wp-validation-docs scope.	fix
10	Runtime discovery is underspecified for the repo's runtime layout. The pin lives under tools/sandbox-runtime/** (work-packages.yaml:78, 87) but skills execute from copied runtime trees (.claude/skills/, .agents/skills/ per AGENTS.md), where a Path(__file__)-relative lookup resolves to a different root; the plan also does not name the explicit override variable, how integrity is checked at dispatch time (package.json version plus package-lock integrity hash of the installed tree), or how `npm ci` for the pin is wired into install.sh/CI. Define the resolution order (explicit absolute override -> repo root via `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` of the dispatcher's own checkout -> unavailable), the metadata checks, and the install step; otherwise every runtime copy will silently take the fail-open path.	fix
11	The execution context carries `location` (dispatch-execution-context.schema.json:20) and the proposal warns that wrapping a submission CLI does not sandbox the remote worker (proposal.md:93-94), but the audit event has no `location` or scope field, so consumers cannot distinguish 'local work sandboxed' from 'cloud submission command sandboxed'. Add `location` and an explicit `enforcement_scope` (execution | submission) to the event and to result metadata.	fix
12	The AST guard (task 4.4, design.md:118-119) has no definition of 'vendor subprocess sink'. 79 non-test skill files call subprocess, and review_dispatcher.py itself has legitimate non-vendor launches (git snapshot handling at 2376-2456, coordinator config query at 2751). Without a precise rule the guard is either noisy or trivially bypassed. Specify the rule: any subprocess/os.exec/asyncio subprocess call in review_dispatcher.py or provider_dispatch.py whose argv derives from cli_config.command, build_command(), poll command_template, or a vendor binary name, outside the backend module, plus an explicit allowlist for the git and coordinator helpers.	fix
13	The scenario 'an attempted write inside or outside the worktree SHALL fail' is not literally achievable with SRT 0.0.77: /tmp/claude, ~/.npm/_logs and ~/.claude/debug remain writable unless denyRead covers them, and the plan grants the runtime temp directory for write modes. Narrow the scenario to the worktree root, HOME credential paths, and a sibling checkout, and have 5.3 document the always-writable paths so the behavioral fixture does not assert a false negative.	fix
openspec/changes/add-dispatch-sandbox-enforcement/reviews/round-1/findings-grok-plan.json
1	Critical: DispatchExecutionContext requires worktree_root, but the plan never specifies who resolves and attaches that canonical root. dg-06 RoutingDispatchContext has no worktree_root field, and autopilot PhaseDispatchPayload only carries isolation (no root, no decision_id). Design D1 says routed callers merely copy the dg-06 assignment, which cannot populate the required root, so implementers cannot build a valid execution context for routed, standalone, or local-provider launches.	fix
2	Critical: Design D5 only says the child environment strips proxy variables, but SRT 0.0.77 skips its resolved-address/domain allowlist checks for connections routed through parentProxy, including HTTP_PROXY/HTTPS_PROXY inherited by the srt process itself. If implementers strip proxies only for the vendor argv after SRT starts, or leave ambient proxies on the env passed to absolute_srt, authored network policy can be bypassed while still reporting applied=true.	fix
3	Critical: Tasks 5.1-5.2 require a controlled vendor fixture and a real capable-host SRT probe with persisted evidence, and design/roadmap acceptance require observable FS/network restriction plus recorded capable-host proof. wp-validation-docs write_allow is only docs/** and openspec trees, so fixture/probe code cannot be landed there, and its verification step only runs openspec validate — a green package does not prove the dg-07 acceptance outcomes.	fix
4	Nit: wp-policy-audit and wp-runtime are parallel (both depends_on: []) yet both include openspec/changes/add-dispatch-sandbox-enforcement/** in write_allow. Parallel packages therefore have overlapping mutable scope for tasks.md/contracts/specs, which the work-package validity rules disallow and which will race during coordinated implementation.	fix
5	Nit: Fail-open durability depends on a mode-0600 local outbox with fsync and later drain, but proposal/design/specs never define the outbox directory, filename scheme, ownership, retention, or crash recovery. Without a fixed path outside the mutable worktree and world-writable temp races, the durable-before-fallback guarantee is not implementable consistently across hosts.	fix
6	Nit: Sandbox audit SHALL not acknowledge durable success until the audit row is inserted, but the existing AuditService.log_operation path returns success=True under async_logging before the insert runs. The plan says synchronous durable audit in tasks 2.4 without explicitly forbidding reuse of that fire-and-forget API, so implementers can satisfy the task text while violating the durable-before-fallback scenario.	fix
7	Nit: vendor-dispatch and design D8 require cancellation to pass through the shared process backend, but CliVendorAdapter has no cancel subprocess sink today — cancelled appears only as an async envelope state observed by poll. The plan therefore over-claims a lifecycle command that does not exist, which will confuse AST-guard and RED/GREEN coverage for cancel.	fix
8	Nit: DispatchExecutionContext allows decision_id null for every source, including source=router, while the routed-execution scenario requires the same decision identifier to appear in execution audit and dg-06 contexts require a non-empty decision_id. The schema therefore admits router-sourced contexts that cannot satisfy the immutability acceptance scenario.	fix
9	Nit: The agent-coordinator sandbox-event requirement says events SHALL include routing correlation, requested/applied isolation, runtime/preflight outcome, policy revision/digest, canonical root, executable paths, environment key names, and degradation reason, but sandbox-execution-event.schema.json leaves decision_id, preflight_status, policy_revision, policy_digest, worktree_root, executable_paths, and degradation_reason optional. Producers can emit schema-valid events that fail the SHALL clause and weaken fail-open observability.	fix
10	Nit: Design D3 rejects roots that are the shared checkout, but does not bind that check to the already-landed skills/shared/checkout_policy.py managed-worktree detector (.git-worktrees/...). Leaving shared-checkout detection unspecified invites a second, divergent heuristic and false accepts/rejects for linked worktrees versus the primary checkout.	fix
11	Optional: network-policy-export.schema.json accepts optional ports via [1-9][0-9]{0,4}, which allows values above 65535 (for example 99999). SRT port suffixes are real TCP ports; invalid ports can either fail closed late or be dropped inconsistently during rendering.	fix
12	FYI: Coordinator SQL matching in is_domain_allowed replaces '*' with SQL LIKE '%' (multi-label), while exported patterns are enforced under SRT wildcard semantics. Operators may see advisory check_domain and sandboxed egress disagree for the same authored pattern; the plan covers deny-first narrowing but not this wildcard-depth mismatch.	accept
13	Post-SRT-start failures correctly fail closed with no unsandboxed retry, and missing/incompatible runtime fail-open only after durable audit/outbox evidence. That closes the double-execution hazard called out in the proposal and matches the Runtime failure never duplicates work scenario.	accept
14	The plan pins @anthropic-ai/sandbox-runtime 0.0.77 with lockfile integrity, forbids dispatch-time install, rejects pre-0.0.16 network-escape versions, and requires a no-op launch preflight before applied=true. That is the right dependency posture for a pre-1.0 enforcement backend.	accept

   222	    """Return a detached routing decision with a canonical dg-05 assignment."""
   223	    decision = copy.deepcopy(dict(value))
   224	    decision_id = decision.get("decision_id")
   225	    assignment = decision.get("assignment")
   226	    if not isinstance(decision_id, str) or not decision_id:
   227	        raise ValueError("routing decision_id must be a non-empty string")
   228	    if not isinstance(assignment, Mapping):
   229	        raise ValueError("routing assignment must be an object")
   230	    required = {"agent_id", "vendor_type", "location", "isolation", "dispatch_mode", "model", "endpoint_kind"}
   231	    if not required.issubset(assignment):
   232	        raise ValueError("routing assignment is missing required fields")
   233	    if any(
   234	        not isinstance(assignment[field], str) or not assignment[field]

   237	        raise ValueError("routing assignment fields must be non-empty strings")

   239	    if isolation not in {"none", "worktree", "sandbox"}:

   241	    return decision

   253	    """Persist and return the immutable context for one routed host dispatch."""
   254	    prior = [

   283	    checkpoint.routing_attempts.append(record)

   285	    return routing

   703	def _report_terminal_capacity(
   704	    result: PhaseDispatchResult,
   705	    reporter: Callable[[PhaseDispatchResult], Any],
   706	) -> None:
   707	    """Report a terminal capacity result without changing the dispatch outcome."""
   708	    error_class = getattr(result.error_class, "value", result.error_class)
   709	    if error_class not in {"capacity", "capacity_exhausted"}:
   710	        return
   711	    try:
   712	        reporter(result)
   713	    except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001 — reporting is best effort
   714	        logger.warning(
   715	            "Provider capacity reporting failed for agent_id=%s: %s",
   716	            result.agent_id,
   717	            exc,
   718	        )

   178	            "provider trust boundary, and dispatches over the OpenAI-compatible "
   179	            "protocol to LOCAL_INFERENCE_BASE_URL in real mode; with that "
   180	            "variable unset or the endpoint unreachable the run reports the "
   181	            "structured fallback degradation instead of hanging. A real-mode run "
   182	            "whose archetype the resolver will not confirm fails without "

   189	    args = parser.parse_args(argv)
   190

   195	        return 2
   196	    except LocalTrustBoundaryError as exc:
   197	        print(f"Local provider trust boundary error: {exc}", file=sys.stderr)
   198	        return 2
   199	
   200	    result = dispatch_phase(payload, dry_run=args.dry_run)
   201	    body = {

   203	        "payload": payload.to_dict(),

   209	        print(

   211	            f"outcome={result.outcome} handoff_id={result.handoff_id} "
   212	            f"tier={result.dispatch_tier}"

     3	Local CLI runs use the shared checkout as an orchestration surface. Mutating

    30	    "isolated_harness",

    38	class CheckoutPolicy:

    54	        return data

    57	class CheckoutPolicyError(RuntimeError):
    58	    """Raised when repository mutation is not allowed from this checkout."""
    59	
    60	    def __init__(self, policy: CheckoutPolicy) -> None:
    61	        super().__init__(policy.message)

    65	def classify_checkout(
    66	    *,
    67	    cwd: Path | str | None = None,
    68	    repo_root: Path | str | None = None,
    69	    sync_point: bool = False,
    70	    agent_id: str | None = None,
    71	) -> CheckoutPolicy:
    72	    """Classify whether repo mutation is allowed from *cwd*.
    73	
    74	    The function does not create worktrees. Callers that need mutation should
    75	    first use ``worktree.py setup`` and then call this guard to verify that the
    76	    resulting checkout is acceptable.
    77	    """
    78	
    79	    resolved_cwd = Path(cwd or Path.cwd()).resolve()
    80	    resolved_repo_root = _resolve_repo_root(resolved_cwd, repo_root)
    81	    profile = environment_profile.detect(agent_id=agent_id)
    82	    worktree_root = _managed_worktree_root(resolved_cwd, resolved_repo_root)
    83	
    84	    if profile.isolation_provided:
    85	        return CheckoutPolicy(
    86	            allowed=True,
    87	            reason="isolated_harness",
    88	            isolation_provided=True,
    89	            cwd=resolved_cwd,
    90	            repo_root=resolved_repo_root,
    91	            worktree_root=worktree_root,
    92	            message=(
    93	                "Mutation allowed: execution environment already provides "
    94	                "filesystem isolation."
    95	            ),
    96	        )
    97	
    98	    if worktree_root is not None:
    99	        return CheckoutPolicy(
   100	            allowed=True,
   101	            reason="managed_worktree",
   102	            isolation_provided=False,
   103	            cwd=resolved_cwd,
   104	            repo_root=resolved_repo_root,
   105	            worktree_root=worktree_root,
   106	            message=f"Mutation allowed inside managed worktree: {worktree_root}",
   107	        )
   108	
   109	    if sync_point:
   110	        return CheckoutPolicy(
   111	            allowed=True,
   112	            reason="approved_sync_point",
   113	            isolation_provided=False,
   114	            cwd=resolved_cwd,
   115	            repo_root=resolved_repo_root,
   116	            worktree_root=None,
   117	            message=(
   118	                "Mutation allowed for explicit sync-point operation. Caller "
   119	                "must still enforce clean-tree and active-agent guards."
   120	            ),
   121	        )
   122	
   123	    return CheckoutPolicy(
   124	        allowed=False,
   125	        reason="shared_checkout_blocked",
   126	        isolation_provided=False,
   127	        cwd=resolved_cwd,
   128	        repo_root=resolved_repo_root,
   129	        worktree_root=None,
   130	        message=(
   131	            "Mutation blocked from local shared checkout. Run worktree.py setup "
   132	            "and perform writes inside the managed worktree, or invoke an "
   133	            "explicit sync-point skill with its clean-tree and active-agent guards."
   134	        ),
   135	    )

   138	def require_mutation_allowed(
   139	    *,
   140	    cwd: Path | str | None = None,
   141	    repo_root: Path | str | None = None,
   142	    sync_point: bool = False,
   143	    agent_id: str | None = None,
   144	) -> CheckoutPolicy:
   145	    """Return the policy or raise when mutation is not allowed."""
   146	
   147	    policy = classify_checkout(
   148	        cwd=cwd,
   149	        repo_root=repo_root,
   150	        sync_point=sync_point,
   151	        agent_id=agent_id,
   152	    )
   153	    if not policy.allowed:
   154	        raise CheckoutPolicyError(policy)
   155	    return policy

   158	def _resolve_repo_root(cwd: Path, repo_root: Path | str | None) -> Path:
   159	    if repo_root is not None:
   160	        return Path(repo_root).resolve()
   161	
   162	    parts = cwd.parts
   163	    if ".git-worktrees" in parts:
   164	        marker_index = parts.index(".git-worktrees")
   165	        if marker_index > 0:
   166	            return Path(*parts[:marker_index]).resolve()
   167	
   168	    git_root = _git_toplevel(cwd)
   169	    if git_root is not None:
   170	        return git_root
   171	    return cwd

   174	def _git_toplevel(cwd: Path) -> Path | None:
   175	    try:
   176	        result = subprocess.run(
   177	            ["git", "rev-parse", "--show-toplevel"],
   178	            cwd=str(cwd),
   179	            check=True,
   180	            capture_output=True,
   181	            text=True,
   182	        )
   183	    except (OSError, subprocess.CalledProcessError):
   184	        return None
   185	    root = result.stdout.strip()
   186	    return Path(root).resolve() if root else None
   187	
   188	
   189	def _managed_worktree_root(cwd: Path, repo_root: Path) -> Path | None:
   190	    marker = repo_root / ".git-worktrees"
   191	    try:
   192	        relative = cwd.relative_to(marker)
   193	    except ValueError:
   194	        return None
   195	
   196	    parts = relative.parts
   197	    if not parts:
   198	        return None
   199	    # Single-agent: .git-worktrees/<change-id>
   200	    # Parallel: .git-worktrees/<change-id>/<agent-id>
   201	    depth = 2 if len(parts) >= 2 and _looks_like_agent_worktree(parts[1]) else 1
   202	    return marker.joinpath(*parts[:depth]).resolve()
   203	
   204	
   205	def _looks_like_agent_worktree(path_part: str) -> bool:
   206	    return path_part.startswith(("wp-", "v")) or path_part in {
   207	        "cleanup",
   208	        "integrator",
   209	    }
   210	
   211	
   212	def _cmd_require_mutation(args: argparse.Namespace) -> int:
   213	    policy = classify_checkout(
   214	        cwd=args.cwd,
   215	        repo_root=args.repo_root,
   216	        sync_point=args.sync_point,
   217	        agent_id=args.agent_id,
   218	    )
   219	    if args.json:
   220	        print(json.dumps(policy.to_jsonable(), indent=2, sort_keys=True))
   221	    elif policy.allowed:
   222	        print(policy.message)
   223	    else:
   224	        print(policy.message, file=sys.stderr)
   225	    return 0 if policy.allowed else 1
   226	
   227	
   228	def _build_parser() -> argparse.ArgumentParser:
   229	    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(
   230	        prog="checkout_policy",
   231	        description="Enforce local shared-checkout mutation policy.",
   232	    )
   233	    sub = parser.add_subparsers(dest="command", required=True)
   234	    require = sub.add_parser(
   235	        "require-mutation",
   236	        help="Exit non-zero unless mutation is allowed from this checkout.",
   237	    )
   238	    require.add_argument("--cwd", default=None, help="Directory to classify.")
   239	    require.add_argument("--repo-root", default=None, help="Shared repository root.")
   240	    require.add_argument("--sync-point", action="store_true")
   241	    require.add_argument("--agent-id", default=None)
   242	    require.add_argument("--json", action="store_true")
   243	    require.set_defaults(func=_cmd_require_mutation)
   244	    return parser
   245	
   246	
   247	def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:
   248	    parser = _build_parser()
   249	    args = parser.parse_args(argv)
   250	    return int(args.func(args))
   251	
   252	
   253	if __name__ == "__main__":
   254	    raise SystemExit(main())

DSE-006	The fail-open audit guarantee is not durable with the existing audit API. The requirement says degradation must be reconstructible from the audit trail alone at `openspec/changes/add-dispatch-sandbox-enforcement/specs/vendor-dispatch/spec.md:56-74`. Yet `AuditService.log_operation()` returns success immediately before insertion when async logging is enabled at `agent-coordinator/src/audit.py:154-160`; `drain()` only checks for pending tasks and never checks failed `AuditResult` values from completed tasks at `audit.py:164-195`; insertion failures merely return a failed result at `audit.py:197-220`. The standalone dispatcher also has no append-audit transport. Define a coordinator-owned, acknowledged sandbox-degradation event contract and a durable fallback spool/replay path so unsandboxed launch cannot lose its evidence during process exit or coordinator/database outage. The dispatcher explicitly resolves common Git metadata outside linked worktrees at `skills/parallel-infrastructure/scripts/review_dispatcher.py:2373-2407` and creates detached fallback worktrees at `review_dispatcher.py:2410-2429`. Specify the Git behavior: for read-only review, set and test `GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS=0` while keeping metadata readable but not writable; for write-capable modes, explicitly decide whether private worktree metadata is denied or narrowly granted without exposing the common repository metadata. The canonical dg-05 `IsolationResolution` contains only `value` and `source` at `agent-coordinator/src/isolation_contract.py:18-22`, so it cannot implicitly carry dg-03 posture. The posture is already implemented as independent booleans at `skills/shared/environment_profile.py:44-94`; this change should consume it rather than reimplement it. Add posture explicitly to the enforcement decision, define behavior for all four filesystem/network combinations, and cover nested-container/runtime-unavailable cases where applying a second filesystem namespace may fail while network enforcement is still required.	fix

   704	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   705	# Driver-facing wiring helper
   706	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

   708	
   709	def make_phase_callback(
   710	    *,
   711	    phase: str,
   712	    subagent_runner: SubagentRunner,
   713	    incoming_handoff_loader: Callable[[str | None], PhaseRecord] | None = None,
   714	    artifacts_manifest: list[str] | None = None,
   715	    coordinator_writer: Any = None,
   716	) -> Callable[[Any], str]:
   717	    """Produce an autopilot-compatible phase callback wrapping run_phase_subagent.
   718	
   719	    The returned callback matches autopilot's existing callback signature
   720	    ``(state) -> outcome`` while internally:
   721	      1. Loading the incoming PhaseRecord from state.last_handoff_id
   722	         (via incoming_handoff_loader, e.g. a coordinator read_handoff).
   723	      2. Calling ``run_phase_subagent`` with the assembled prompt scaffold.
   724	      3. Mutating ``state.last_handoff_id`` and ``state.handoff_ids`` with
   725	         the returned handoff_id.
   726	      4. Returning ONLY the outcome string to the driver.
   727	
   728	    This realizes Layer 2 — the driver-side LoopState delta after the
   729	    callback returns is bounded to ``last_handoff_id`` + one new entry in
   730	    ``handoff_ids``. The sub-agent's transcript stays inside this module.
   731	
   732	    Args:
   733	        phase: Phase id to dispatch (e.g. "IMPLEMENT").
   734	        subagent_runner: Runner that invokes the harness Agent tool.
   735	        incoming_handoff_loader: ``Callable[[handoff_id | None], PhaseRecord]``
   736	            used to hydrate the previous phase's record. The default loader
   737	            constructs an empty bootstrap record when last_handoff_id is None
   738	            (typical at the very first transition).
   739	        artifacts_manifest: Optional repo-relative paths to include in the
   740	            standard prompt scaffold.
   741	        coordinator_writer: Forwarded to run_phase_subagent for the failure
   742	            path's phase-failed record.
   743	
   744	    Returns:
   745	        ``(state) -> outcome`` callable suitable for use as
   746	        ``implement_fn``, ``validate_fn``, or the IMPL_REVIEW phase wrapper
   747	        in autopilot.run_loop.
   748	    """
   749	    loader = incoming_handoff_loader or _default_incoming_loader
   750	
   751	    def callback(state: Any) -> str:
   752	        last_id = getattr(state, "last_handoff_id", None)
   753	        incoming = loader(last_id)
   754	        state_change_id = getattr(state, "change_id", None)
   755	        if incoming.change_id == "" and isinstance(state_change_id, str) and state_change_id:
   756	            incoming.change_id = state_change_id
   757	
   758	        state_dict = _state_snapshot(state)
   759	        outcome, handoff_id = run_phase_subagent(
   760	            phase=phase,
   761	            state_dict=state_dict,
   762	            incoming_handoff=incoming,
   763	            subagent_runner=subagent_runner,
   764	            artifacts_manifest=artifacts_manifest,
   765	            coordinator_writer=coordinator_writer,
   766	        )
   767	        # Bounded driver-side state delta — D6
   768	        state.last_handoff_id = handoff_id
   769	        if hasattr(state, "handoff_ids"):
   770	            state.handoff_ids.append(handoff_id)
   771	        # D7: propagate the archetype name resolved by _build_options into
   772	        # LoopState.phase_archetype for audit/observability. Override path
   773	        # and bridge-failure path leave _resolved_archetype unset, so we
   774	        # explicitly null the field for those cases (so downstream
   775	        # observability surfaces "default-fallback" phases).
   776	        if hasattr(state, "phase_archetype"):
   777	            state.phase_archetype = state_dict.get("_resolved_archetype")
   778	        return outcome
   779	
   780	    return callback
   781	
   782	
   783	def _default_incoming_loader(handoff_id: str | None) -> PhaseRecord:
   784	    """Bootstrap loader — returns an empty PhaseRecord when no prior handoff.
   785	
   786	    Production use should pass a loader that calls ``read_handoff`` against
   787	    the coordinator (or reads the local fallback file) and returns a
   788	    hydrated PhaseRecord. This default exists so make_phase_callback works
   789	    in tests without coordinator access.
   790	    """

   587	check_openspec_cli() {
   588	  local mode="$1"
   589	
   590	  if [[ "$mode" == "none" ]]; then

   621	      return 1

   632	    return 1

   636	    return 0
   637	  fi
